/species/caputitermes-dimorphus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The primary genus character is the dimorphic worker (major worker and minor worker); the junction between the midgut and the first proctodeal segment (P1) is straight, without a mixed segment; the molar plate and molar prominence region bear hairs and scale-like sculpture; the gizzard is not developed; the inner wall of P1 is densely covered with short, stout spines directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped bend before joining P2. No Neotropical Apicotermitinae have soldiers.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the major and minor workers in a ratio of about 1:2, both forms common. Both have a visible fontanelle, a slightly inflated postclypeus and a head covered with fine short setae; the mandibles bear hairs and scale-like sculpture on the molar plate and molar prominence region, with a shallow concavity on the anterior side of the mandible; the apical tooth of the left mandible is as large as marginal teeth 1 and 2 combined, and the apical tooth of the right mandible is larger than marginal teeth 1 and 2 combined. Major worker: head capsule square, with about 34 setae, mainly distributed on the anterolateral and posterior regions, the head with lateral nodes; minor worker: head capsule round, with about 14 setae evenly distributed on the sides of the head. The gut is spherical in both forms, and the structures are similar in size and position. Gizzard without cuticular armature, with 6 primary pulvilli, the pulvilli scaly on the surface and with minute spines posteriorly; enteric valve with a thin muscle layer and 6 symmetrical cushions; Malpighian tubules with 4 separate insertions, without a nodule; the short stout spines of the P1 inner wall are densest near the midgut and near P2, with the spine tips directed towards the enteric valve; P3 forms an S-shaped bend before joining P2. Measurements: species-level (LH, WH, LT, WP, see the species description).

/species/cephalotermes-rectangularis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, containing only Cephalotermes rectangularis (Sjöst.), from Cameroon and Congo. The soldier has a rectangular, flattened-cylindrical head without eyes and 12 antennal segments; the worker mandibles are of a modified Termes type (Hamitermes type) and its antennae have 13 segments; the alate has 14 antennal segments, segment 1 very large and segment 3 small, spiny wings, and no exudate hairs in the female. Holmgren's original description is based on the queen (a dealate) and points out that, judging from the size of its head and thorax, the alate itself should be fairly small.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The original describes this caste from the queen (Königin). The head is oval and slightly narrowed anteriorly. The frons is flatly convex, slightly depressed in front of the frontal gland pore. The compound eyes are medium-sized and fairly flat; the ocelli are medium-sized and slightly lateral, almost no more than their larger diameter from the compound eyes. The frontal gland pore is small and distinct, situated in the middle of the head. The base of the clypeus is moderately raised and almost as long as half its width, its posterior margin fairly strongly convex and its anterior margin straight and clearly delimited, brighter than the frons. The labrum is wider than long. The mandibular base is small; the mandibles are of Termes type, the basal tooth of the left mandible weakly developed. There are 14 antennal segments, segment 1 very large and segment 3 small. The pronotum is only slightly narrower than the head: head width 0.79 mm, pronotum width 0.7 mm. The posterior margins of the meso- and metanota are emarginate, the posterior projections blunt and rounded. The forewing scale is distinctly longer than the hindwing scale, and the wing surface bears small spines. The female has no exudate hairs; the sides of the queen's abdomen are warty, somewhat wrinkled and weakly pigmented. Because its abdomen is extremely developed, the queen described is unusually large.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is rectangular and flattened-cylindrical. The frons is slightly inclined. There are no eyes, and the coronal suture is invisible. The frontal gland pore is almost unrecognisable, and the frontal gland is very indistinct and small. The clypeus is lens-shaped; the labrum is quadrangular with rounded anterior corners. The mandibles are short and robust with a large base; the middle part bears 2 small teeth on each side; the base of the left mandible has one small tooth, and the base of the right mandible is mainly rounded. The antennae are slender, with 12 segments, segment 3 shorter and narrower than segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4. The pronotum is fairly small and saddle-shaped, with a fairly short anterior lobe. The cerci are small; there are no styli. The fore tibia bears 3 apical spurs, the mid and hind tibiae 2 each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Small. The head is oval, fairly thick, flattened and raised; the frontal gland pore is fairly far back. The base of the clypeus is longer than half its width and raised, its posterior margin very strongly arched and clearly delimited, its anterior margin straight. The labrum is small and strongly inclined, wider in the middle than at the base. The mandibles are of a modified Termes type (Hamitermes type). There are 13 antennal segments, segment 3 far shorter and narrower than segment 2 and distinctly shorter than segment 4. The pronotum is short, far narrower than the head and saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe almost as long as the posterior part. The cerci are short; there are no styli. The original adds: the Malpighian tubules have no collecting vesicle, and hindgut segments I–II have no glandular plates.

/species/ceratokalotermes-spoliator/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is closest to Paraneotermes and Comatermes; it differs from Comatermes in the absence of long, undulate setae on the head and pronotum; in Paraneotermes the posterior margins of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible have a distinct flexure and the arolium is absent; in both these genera the soldier mandibles are short and stout, the frontal dorsal processes are very weak or absent, and the anterior margin of the pronotum is not deeply concave.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; eye small, about 0.25 mm in diameter, the ocellus touching the compound eye; antennal segments 13–14; the posterior margins of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible as long as the anterior margin of marginal tooth 3; the molar plate of the right mandible nearly as long as the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2; pronotum broader than the head, anterior margin concave; radial vein of the forewing usually branched, the radial sector with 7–8 branches, the first about 1/6 of the wing length from the wing suture; media weakly sclerotised, closer to the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head somewhat shield-like in frontal view, narrow, the sides parallel; antennal carinae large and distinctly projecting; frontal concavity steeply sloping to the clypeus; anterior dorsal surface with two large swellings or lobes, forming a uniform arc between the lobes; eye colourless; antennal segments 11–14, the third not specialised, about as long as the second; mandibles long and slender; pronotum as broad as the head, transversely arched, the anterior margin raised with a deep angular concavity, with a median notch; legs short and stout.

/species/coendutermes-tucum/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the dorsal surface and sides of the head bear many scattered hollow glandular setae that are stout, brown and truncate at the tip; apart from the tip of the nasus the head has no ordinary setae; the nasus is conical, slightly curved upwards and pointed at the apex; the antennae are very long and extend far beyond the tip of the nasus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; the dorsal surface and sides of the head capsule bear many scattered hollow glandular setae that are large, erect, brown and truncate at the tip; apart from the tip of the nasus the head has no ordinary setae; the nasus is conical, slightly curved upwards and pointed at the apex; the postclypeus is weakly inclined and visible in dorsal view; the apex of each mandible bears a separate projection but no well-developed apical point; the antennae are very long and extend far beyond the tip of the nasus.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Apparently monotypic; the abdominal sclerites are pale or colourless and transparent, so that the gut contents show through; there are no glandular setae; the head bears a few long setae and many of medium length; the postclypeus is moderately inflated, width/length 2.90–3.25.

/species/comatermes-perfectus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus; the alate wing venation resembles that of Paraneotermes and Ceratokalotermes, but the head and pronotum bear very long, fine, slightly undulate setae; the soldier differs from Ceratokalotermes, in which the anterior dorsal surface of the head has two distinct lobes and the anterior margin of the pronotum is raised and deeply concave, and from Paraneotermes, whose mandibles are short and stout.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; head and pronotum with very long, fine, slightly undulate setae; eye small, 0.29–0.31 mm in diameter, the ocellus touching the compound eye; antennal segments 14; the posterior margins of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible as long as the anterior margin of marginal tooth 3; pronotum broader than the head; radial sector with 9–10 branches; media less strongly sclerotised than the radial sector, with many cross-veins between it and the radial sector; arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head usually long, sometimes long-headed and short-headed forms occurring in the same species; head flattened dorsoventrally; frontal concavity central, the anterior part hollowed, the anterior dorsal surface with two weak swellings; eye colourless; antennal segments 13–14, the third not specialised, as long as the second; mandibles stout, relatively short for the head length; pronotum as broad as the head, the anterior margin shallowly and broadly concave; femora inflated.

/species/cornicapritermes-mucronatus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with Paracapritermes, Mirocapritermes and Quasitermes, the mandibular asymmetry of the soldier is stronger and marginal tooth 2 of the worker is less distinct; Emerson (1950) considered Paracapritermes the most generalised of the four, Mirocapritermes next, Quasitermes next, and Cornicapritermes the most specialised.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is thick and long, its sides slightly curved; the conical frontal projection points forwards, extends far beyond the mandibular bases, is slightly upturned at its tip, and bears a small swelling before and below the tip that appears to be the opening of the fontanelle.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical tooth is distinctly larger than marginal tooth 1; marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible is reduced or absent; on the left mandible there is a small notch between marginal tooth 3 and the fused marginal teeth 1 and 2.

/species/crepititermes-verruculosus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the frons is flat, clearly different from that of the other groups of Mirotermes (at that time a broad genus containing this group); apart from this it is closest to the subgenus Mirotermes s. str.; the mandibles are of the snapping type and shaped as in Mirotermes s. str.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is brown and broadly oval, densely covered with short hairs and setae; the fontanelle is slightly deeper than the rest of the head capsule and inconspicuous; the left mandible has 2 large teeth (one pointed, one rounded) and the right mandible only 1 pointed tooth; segment 3 of the antennae is extremely short, far shorter than segment 4.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is pale yellow and covered with short hairs, elongate and nearly rectangular, its sides nearly parallel, narrowing sharply in front of the antennal bases; the antennae are paler than the head and 13-segmented; the labrum has 2 points; the mandibles are brown and slender, sharply curved at the apex, broad at the base and toothed on the inner margin (more markedly so on the left than on the right); the pronotum is paler than the head and saddle-shaped.

/species/disjunctitermes-insularis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the Neotropical apicotermitines, like Anoplotermes banksi, A. pacificus and Hydrecotermes spp., it has a strongly inflated fore tibia and an enteric valve without spines or sclerotisation. It is closest to A. banksi but distinguished by the accessory (fourth) marginal tooth of the left mandible, the larger enteric valve seating and the more truncate end of P2; Hydrecotermes lacks a spherical mesenteric tongue.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, small. Head capsule pale yellow, with about 100 setae of varying length; postclypeus moderately inflated; fontanelle almost indiscernible; antennal segments 14. The apical tooth of the left mandible is widely separated from marginal tooth 1, both long, clearly exceeding the line joining marginal tooth 3 and the molar prominence; above the molar prominence there is an additional accessory (fourth) marginal tooth, visible in both dorsal and ventral view. The apical tooth of the right mandible is much longer than marginal tooth 1, and marginal tooth 3 is nearly symmetrical. Fore tibia strongly inflated, about 3 times as long as its greatest (median) width. Mesenteric tongue spherical. P2 enters through a large, stout trilobed enteric valve seating, two lobes of which are visible through the body wall; the enteric valve consists of 6 slender, inflated pads facing the valve lumen; the posterior end of P2 (including the enteric valve) is truncate, extending about halfway into the seating. Measurements: species-level (Table 2, 12 workers from each of 11 colonies; holotype head width 0.64 mm).

/species/ebogotermes-raphaeli/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The largest of the soldierless apicotermitine workers of equatorial Africa; it is assigned to the Anoplotermes group on the basis of the looped midgut, the well-developed mixed segment, the moderately long P1, the P3/P4 constriction and the long tubular P4.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head, thorax, abdomen and legs are covered with setae of varying length; there are 14 antennal segments; the postclypeus is moderately inflated; the fore tibia is slightly inflated; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/species/echinotermes-biriba/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The crop is unusually large, and the enteric valve consists of 6 globular comb-like cushions whose ends are spinous spheres; this combination is unique among the genera of the Apicotermitinae.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; the head and antennae are pale yellow, the pronotum pale yellow and the legs transparent. The crop is very large; the EVS is trilobed, the smaller lobe being invisible in the intact gut; the enteric valve has 6 cushions whose ends form spinous spheres at the opening into P3.

/species/ekueitermes-alerosinus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The mesenteric tongue of the mixed segment is short and not inflated; P1 is very short; the enteric valve armature (EVA) consists of 6 conical cushions each covered with 18–25 fringed polygonal scales (4–15 per cushion), with 7–17 sclerotised spines at the distal end of each cushion arranged in a palmate fashion; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is distinctly differentiated and tubular.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (head length and width from medium to large). Head capsule pale white to pale yellow, densely covered with long, fine, pale, erect setae evenly spaced, with short hairs between them; dorsal surface slightly concave in profile; antennal segments translucent. Antennal segments 14, pattern 2>3<4<5. Fontanelle distinct, oval, situated behind the brain (visible in preserved specimens); postclypeus strongly inflated. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior and posterior margins with rows of long, fine, erect setae, the lateral margins with a few long setae; the margins of the anterior lobes of the meso- and metanotum also with setal rows. Abdomen translucent, the tergites and sternites densely covered with setae of varying length. Fore coxa and fore femur with numerous pale fine setae; fore tibia strongly inflated, with a few long setae interspersed among a great many minute, dense setae; tibial spines weak on all legs, indistinct except at the apex; spur formula 2:2:2. Apical tooth of the left mandible more projecting than M1+2, forming an acute angle with it, the posterior margin of M1+2 weakly concave; M3 less projecting than M1+2, its margin forming an acute angle; molar prominence well developed, not concealing the molar process in dorsal view. Right mandible: apical tooth more projecting than M1, M1 small and slightly exceeding M2, a right angle between M1 and M2, the posterior margin of M2 concave, without ridges. Gut: crop large; mixed segment short and not inflated; midgut short and slender, gradually widening into a very short, tubular P1 that does not form a ventral loop; EVS well differentiated, tubular; P3 large and inflated, P4 very long and slender, P5 saccular. Measurements: species-level (Table 1, 17 workers from 3 colonies).

/species/eleanoritermes-borneensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus (Eleanoritermes borneensis Ahmad, Borneo). It resembles Niuginitermes, but the enteric valve is situated further forwards and its 3 swellings bear only a few small spines and are weakly armed; the Malpighian tubules are inserted close together.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: There are 11 antennal segments; the mandibles are toothless (without a point).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: There are 12 antennal segments; the enteric valve is situated relatively far forwards, its 3 swellings weakly armed, and the Malpighian tubules are inserted close together (see the diagnostic characters).

/species/emersonitermes-thekadensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A monotypic genus endemic to southern India. The soldier head capsule is creamy white and pear-shaped, the nasus reddish brown, slender and conical, the mandibles reduced and spineless, the antennae 14-segmented, the pronotum saddle-shaped with a non-emarginate anterior margin, and each abdominal tergite bears 4 long hairs; the worker has 13 antennal segments and a large basal process on the left mandible that projects beyond marginal tooth 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head capsule is creamy white, the frontal gland area paler; the nasus is reddish brown; the antennae are brown; the pronotum is yellow; the legs and abdomen are creamy white. The head capsule is pear-shaped and densely covered with minute hairs interspersed with long ones; the nasus is slender and conical; there are 14 antennal segments; the mandibles are reduced and spineless; the pronotum is saddle-shaped with a non-emarginate anterior margin; the apical tibial spur formula is 2:2:2 and the tarsi are 4-segmented; the abdomen is elongate, each tergite bearing 4 long hairs.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head capsule is nearly circular and densely haired; the coronal suture is invisible; the frontal plate is elliptical and white; there are 13 antennal segments; the postclypeus is raised and half as long as wide; the mandibles have an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth; the apical tooth of the left mandible is sharp and nearly as long as marginal tooth 1; marginal tooth 1 is large, narrow and triangular with a long posterior margin; marginal tooth 2 is small and widely separated; the basal process is large and projects beyond marginal tooth 2; on the right mandible the apical tooth is nearly as long as marginal tooth 1; marginal tooth 1 is isosceles-triangular; marginal tooth 2 is short, with the posterior margin longer than the anterior, and the angle between the two marginal teeth is obtuse; the molar plate is longer than the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2; the pronotum and legs are as in the soldier.

/species/engelitermes-zambo/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In overall soldier morphology the closest termites in the world are the African Cephalotermes and the Neotropical Cylindrotermes, but the soldier gut of this genus contains no solid food particles (white-gutted in the original), which distinguishes it from both; its soldiers are consistently smaller than the mandibulate soldiers of the African Termitinae, comparable in size to Forficulitermes planifrons (maximum head width 0.63 mm versus 0.65 mm), but the inner mandible shape is entirely different. The worker mandibles are of the soil-/humus-feeding type, whereas those of Cephalotermes and Cylindrotermes workers are of the wood-feeding type: apical tooth broad, widely separated from marginal tooth 1, molar region concave and without ridges (similar to Crenetermes, Eutermellus, Jugositermes and Thoracotermes); it is especially similar to the worker of Forficulitermes in the wide gap between the apical tooth and marginal tooth 1, and in the well-developed first and fourth hindgut segments. The combination of a single spine with unsculptured pad cuticle in the enteric valve is unique among termite enteric valves; the gizzard is simplified relative to most Termitinae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Described from 1 physogastric queen only: head brown, bearing several hundred setae of varying length, mostly directed forwards and arising from hyaline sockets; the median branch of the frontal suture darker than the rest of the head; fontanelle small, round, situated between the ocelli; the anterolateral part of the head with two crescent-shaped patches in front of the fontanelle. Pronotum and postclypeus paler than the vertex, with similar pilosity; postclypeus not inflated. The antennae of the specimen examined are broken, but with more than 10 segments; segments 3 and 4 almost fused, segment 3 shorter than segment 2, segments 3 and 4 together longer than segment 2. Inner mandibular apical tooth narrower than in the worker. Spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule subrectangular in dorsal view, the lateral margins slightly converging posteriorly; in profile the frontal surface is raised and undulating near the fontanelle; fontanelle small, almost indiscernible; inner mandibles robust, with 1 triangular tooth at the base; antennal segments 12; the anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum congruent, together forming a straight-line triangle in profile; spur formula 2:2:2; abdomen yellowish white, the gut containing no solid food residues (white-gutted sensu Scheffrahn et al. 2017).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: A large white brain (supraoesophageal ganglion) is visible through the head capsule in dorsal view, in front of the small diamond-shaped frontal gland tissue; in profile the postclypeus is slightly inflated. Inner mandibular apical tooth broad and projecting; the gap between the apical tooth and marginal tooth 1 of the left inner mandible is greater than the distance between marginal teeth 1 and 3; molar region concave, without ridges. Antennal segments 12; spur formula 2:2:2; fore femur slightly inflated. Gizzard lacking the columnar belt, the pulvillar belt with sclerotised spinules, beneath which lie patches of ridge-like scales. Enteric valve composed of 6 smooth, slender pads, each with 1 small spine at its distal end, the pads pointing with the food stream; the enteric valve armature (EVA) has 1 slightly sclerotised pad in front of the ring, bearing 1–2 stout spines and several small spines. Mixed segment absent. Ileum cylindrical, running in a long S along the left side of the abdomen, narrowing posteriorly and folding forwards to meet P2; P4 broad anteriorly and narrow posteriorly; P5 unusually large in volume (but not in all individuals).

/species/euscaiotermes-primus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus endemic to India. Soldier: head subrectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly, antennae 17-segmented (segment 3 shorter than segment 2), labrum triangular with a pointed apex, mandibles stout with incurved apices, left mandible with a notch behind the apical third, right mandible without teeth; worker: antennae 19-segmented, postclypeus one-third as long as wide, mandibles of the Odontotermes type.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head subrectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly; antennae 17-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2; labrum triangular with a pointed apex; mandibles stout, apices incurved; left mandible with a notch behind the apical third, right mandible without teeth; postmentum subrectangular; pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin notched, posterior margin slightly concave; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented; cerci 2-segmented; with a small spinous process.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head subcircular, wider than long; frontal gland pore white, circular, large; antennae 19-segmented; postclypeus raised, one-third as long as wide; mandibles of the Odontotermes type, with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth; pronotum saddle-shaped; legs as in the soldier.

/species/fastigitermes-jucundus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the front of the head covers the mandibular bases, contrary to Basidentitermes, where it does not; Emerson (1928) treated M. jucundus provisionally as a subgenus of Mirotermes and agreed with Sjöstedt in giving it a separate genus, Fastigitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The elevation of the vertex above the opening of the fontanelle extends further forwards; compared with Profastigitermes the backward projection of the postmentum is proportionally much larger and ends in a single, fairly sharp backward-pointing spine.

/species/firmitermes-abyssinicus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closely related to Hoplognathotermes, with no genus-level difference in head shape, but the pilosity of the head surface, postmentum and fore coxa is far richer, the postmentum is transversely wrinkled along its whole length, the labrum is broad and rounded, without lateral angles or points, and the mandibular base is short and stout; the alate is described only from the provisionally assigned 'Eutermes' tripolitanus, whose left marginal tooth 3 is proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the primitive termite subfamily or of the Amitermitinae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The following genus characters presuppose the provisional assignment of 'Eutermes' tripolitanus to this genus. The apical teeth of both mandibles are smaller and more slender than in workers of Hoplognathotermes and Acutidentitermes, and lie closer to marginal tooth 1; the angle between the apical tooth and marginal tooth 1 of the left mandible is sharper; the actual lengths of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible are similar to those of Acutidentitermes, but the notch before marginal tooth 3 is less sharp and the apical margin of marginal tooth 3 is longer (distinctly convex and short in Acutidentitermes); marginal tooth 3 is proportionally far larger than in any known genus of the primitive termite subfamily or of the Amitermitinae; beneath the concave ridge between marginal tooth 3 and the molar plate of the left mandible there are 2 small processes, with a concave margin between them (Acutidentitermes has only 1 process below the basal molar plate); marginal tooth 1 of the right mandible shows a vestige of an accessory tooth near its angle of contact with the apical tooth; the anterior and posterior margins of marginal tooth 2 are both concave, whereas in Acutidentitermes it is convex-blunt with nearly straight margins; the concavity on the upper margin of the basal plate of the right mandible is weaker than in Acutidentitermes. Each fore tibia with 3 spurs, each mid and hind tibia with 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface, vertex, sides and postmentum scattered with numerous short hairs and setae, whereas Hoplognathotermes subterraneus and Acutidentitermes osborni have very few setae on the head surface and an almost hairless postmentum. The profile of the flattened-convex distal part of the fore coxa shows 3–4 setae, the profile of the acute-convex basal part bears a few setae and short hairs, the longitudinal ridge is bluntly rounded, and a few extremely short hairs are visible when the coxa is rotated. Head shape shows no genus-level difference from Hoplognathotermes, the anterior part flatter, without conspicuous ridges or tubercles; fontanelle small and indistinct. Postmentum constricted in the middle, the sides rather concave (slightly deeper than in Hoplognathotermes), with a series of indistinct transverse wrinkles along its whole length; in H. subterraneus only the posterior part is transversely wrinkled, and in A. osborni the postmentum is globular and unwrinkled. Labrum proportionally as broad as in H. subterraneus but with more rounded margins, lacking the lateral angles and points of the latter or of A. osborni. Postclypeus distinct, the suture between it and the frons not obliterated. Mandibular base proportionally short and stout, the outer margin rather strongly convex, without the angular notch at the junction of tip and base seen in Hoplognathotermes or Acutidentitermes; the apical process shorter and stouter than in either, the outer margin more curved; in the type specimen the tooth bases are broken, so the tooth form cannot be determined, but the small notch between the apical margin and the tooth of the right mandible indicates an angle close to that of H. subterraneus and unlike the sharper angle of A. osborni; the basal tooth-like process indistinct or absent. Pronotum smaller and narrower than in H. subterraneus, the anterior lobe equally large, the median anterior concavity equally small and shallow; the angle between the anterior lobe and the posterior part in lateral view less sharp than in H. subterraneus, nearly flatly concave. Fore coxa without a process, the longitudinal ridge rather bluntly rounded, not as sharp and long as in H. subterraneus; the ridge profile is flatly convex from the trochanteral region to the middle and becomes flatly concave towards the basal outer corner. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the outer spur extremely short, visible only on careful manipulation; mid and hind tibiae each with 2 spurs.

/species/forficulitermes-planifrons/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier labrum has two lateral points and a distinctly projecting median lobe, on which basis it is allied to Basidentitermes, Proboscitermes, Orthotermes, Profastigitermes and Fastigitermes; it is a small and peculiar group that branched off near Basidentitermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In dorsal view the head is nearly square, its sides almost straight or slightly convex, and the frons and vertex flatter than in related genera; the frontal gland lies in a small depression, and on each side in front of its opening there are two flat longitudinal ridges; the front of the labrum bears two lateral points and a distinctly projecting median lobe; the mandibles are of the biting type, relatively straight and slender, not hooked at the apex; the base of the left mandible has a small sharp tooth followed by a deep, small angular bend ending in a spine-like projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The mandibles resemble those of the more primitive groups near Basidentitermes; the apical tooth is larger than marginal tooth 1; the right mandible has a distinct marginal tooth 2.

/species/gastrotermes-spinatus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It is assigned to the Apicotermes group on the basis of the absence of a mixed segment, the very short P1 and the large, trilobed EVS. It differs from the other genera of the Labidotermes subgroup in that the inner wall of the EVS bears small erect spines and the opening of P3a is lined with stout spines. The alate is unknown; the soldier is unknown (the original records 'Soldier. Unknown, but may exist').

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head, pronotum and abdomen are densely covered with several hundred long to very long hairs.

/species/genuotermes-spinifer/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the mandibles are elongate and bent at a distinct elbow in the proximal 1/3, the inner margin of the distal 2/3 forming a serrate blade with a basal projecting tooth, and the molar plate and molar prominence visible at the base; the head capsule is nearly rectangular in dorsal view with a characteristic frontal projection, the opening of the frontal gland lying at the end of the head projection and facing forwards. In the alate the compound eyes are hemispherical and the fontanelle is a small slit.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The mandibles are elongate and bent at the elbow in the proximal 1/3; the inner margin of the distal 2/3 forms a serrate blade, with a conspicuous projecting tooth at the base; the molar plate and molar prominence are visible at the base. The head capsule is nearly rectangular in dorsal view, with a characteristic frontal projection (best seen in profile); the opening of the frontal gland lies at the end of the head projection and faces forwards. The labrum is nearly rectangular; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head capsule is circular in dorsal view; the fontanelle is indistinct; there are 14–15 antennal segments; the apical tooth of the mandibles is far more developed than the marginal teeth, whose apices are discernible. Digestive tract: P1 is inflated and lies on the left side of the body, its last section forming an elongate loop that reaches the dorsal region and then descends into P3; the columnar band of the gizzard has 24 visible folds (6 first-order, 6 second-order, 12 third-order), the first-order folds bearing spine-like ornamentation; the enteric valve consists of three equidistant longitudinal cushions covered with stout erect spines in a brush-like arrangement.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The compound eyes are hemispherical, elliptical in profile, approaching but not touching the lower margin of the head and the ocelli; the fontanelle is indistinct, forming a small slit on the dorsal surface of the head; the pronotum is nearly trapezoidal with rounded anterolateral corners; the posterior margin of the mesonotum is deeply emarginate and pointed, that of the metanotum shallower and rounded; tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

/species/hirsutitermes-kanzakii/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The posterior margin of the enteric valve armature bears several hundred fine spines; the enteric valve seating (EVS) is tubular, trilobed and long; the mesenteric tongue is long but not inflated. Closest to Longustitermes: the spines of this genus are longer and finer than in the latter, and the anterior portion of the cushions is pyriform (the original reads 'the anterior portion of the cushions is more rounded in the latter than pyriform in the former'); Longustitermes is smaller, and its EVS is trilobed rather than tubular.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule forming a very gentle curve in profile. Fontanelle distinct, heart-shaped, situated near the imaginary line of the posterior margin of the compound eye and behind the oval patch (= median clypeal muscle). Above the antennal sockets there are two distinct oval patches. Antennal segments 12, pattern 2>3<4≈5. Pronotum with a distinct median suture and a raised anterior margin.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic, medium-sized (body and head from medium to large). Head capsule pale yellow, densely covered with long hairs and sparse, slightly larger setae, the dorsal surface flat in profile. Antennal segments translucent white; 14 segments, pattern 2>3=4<5. Fontanelle round, distinct but with indistinct margins; postclypeus moderately inflated. Pronotum with very long setae, especially on the middle of the anterior and posterior lobes; tergites and sternites with short hairs on the surface and long setae on the posterior margins. Fore coxa and fore femur with medium-sized spines; fore tibia moderately inflated, densely covered with spines and setae of various sizes. Apical tooth of the left mandible more projecting than M1+2; the two margins of M3 forming an obtuse angle, the tip slightly rounded and directed forwards; molar process distinct, not concealed by the molar prominence; molar prominence well developed. Right mandible: apical tooth much more projecting than M1, M1 small and less projecting than M2, the margin of M2 curved; molar plate concave with a few ridges. Gut: mesenteric tongue long and not inflated; EVS relatively long and tubular, usually with three small but distinct lobes; the junction of P3-a and the seating visible in dorsal view; armature with several hundred fine, elongated sclerotised spines, distributed from the fourth distal part of the enteric valve onwards. Measurements: species-level (Table 2).

/species/hoplotermes-amplus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head width greater than 1.8 mm; the mandibles are robust and shorter than the head width; the mandibular bases arise near the anterolateral corners of the head, and the inner margin is smooth.

/species/hyleotermes-brevipilus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule oval in dorsal view, with a long cylindrical nasus, without a constriction and without long setae, covered with microscopic hairs; worker slightly dimorphic, the mixed segment very short; enteric valve with 6 pads of unequal size, each bearing from a few to several dozen narrow spines set on conical bases. In its small size, pale yellow colour and cylindrical nasus the soldier is closest to Ereymatermes and Subulitermes; of the three, only H. brevipilus, S. constricticeps and S. microsoma lack long setae on the head capsule, and the latter two are distinctly smaller (head width about 0.6 mm). The worker enteric valve is diagnostic and differs from Ereymatermes and Subulitermes. It differs from Nasutitermes s. str. as follows: the latter has an enteric valve armature with acute scales drawn backwards into scale rows, a narrow straight molar plate with well-developed ridges, short apical teeth and larger marginal teeth on the inner mandibles, a very long mixed segment, and an unclerotised enteric valve with only spinules; moreover, female workers of Nasutitermes s. str. are distinctly larger than males.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eye large, somewhat oval; ocellus large, elliptical, about as large as the antennal socket; postclypeus slightly arched in profile, the midline distinct and slightly concave, the anterior margin nearly straight, the posterior margin convex; fontanelle distinct, slit-like; frontal suture faint; antennal segments 15; inner mandibular tooth pattern similar to that of worker morph 2; pronotum trapezoidal in dorsal view, the anterior and posterior margins nearly straight; the posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum deeply and broadly concave, the posterolateral corners rounded; spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; head capsule longer than wide in dorsal view, without a constriction; nasus slender, almost cylindrical; head capsule, legs and thoracic sclerites densely covered with short, rather coarse setae; inner mandibles with a small but distinct 'point'; antennal segments 12; postclypeus not convex in profile; labrum wider than long, the anterior margin rounded, the sides parallel, the anterolateral corners rounded; anterior and posterior pronotal lobes equally developed, forming an obtuse angle between them; fore coxa conical, not forming a ridge, without a boss on the anterior surface; spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, the two morphs similar in size. In morph 1 the gap between M3 and the molar prominence of the left inner mandible is narrow, the head capsule darker and nearly trapezoidal, and the pronotum narrower with the anterior lobe larger than the posterior; in morph 2 the gap is wide, the head capsule slightly paler with more convex sides, and the pronotum broader with the anterior and posterior lobes nearly equal. In both morphs the fontanelle lies in the posterior half of the head capsule, is pale and slightly concave in profile; postclypeus not inflated; antennal segments 13; spur formula 2:2:2. In both morphs the apical tooth of the left inner mandible is larger than M1, the posterior margin of the apical tooth slightly concave, the posterior margin of the apical tooth forming an acute angle with the anterior margin of M1, and the posterior margin of M1 undulate; M3 short but distinct, with a V-shaped gap to the molar prominence in morph 1 and a wide gap in morph 2; M4 short, hidden beneath the molar prominence; molar prominence concave with faint ridges. Right inner mandible: apical tooth larger than M1, M3 reduced with a rounded end, the posterior margin of M3 concave, the molar plate concave with faint ridges, the basal notch distinct but narrower in morph 2.

/species/indocapritermes-aruni/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Couplets 9–10 of the Oriental key: head moderately haired and frons inclined forwards → the anterolateral corners of the labrum minute and slender with a narrow base, the anterior lobe of the pronotum slightly convex with a weak notch, and 14 antennal segments. It differs from Rinacapritermes in the anterolateral corners of the labrum long and robust with a wide base, the anterior lobe of the pronotum strongly convex and without a notch, and 15 antennal segments.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is moderately haired, and the frons is distinctly inclined forwards; the anterolateral corners of the labrum are minute and slender with a narrow base; the anterior lobe of the pronotum is slightly convex with a weak notch; there are 14 antennal segments. The middle of the left mandible is strongly twisted and its tip blunt.

/species/jugositermes-tuberculatus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: frons steeply inclined (about 45°), two distinct ridges above the antennal bases, the antennal bases set in a groove at one end; left mandible with a small tooth; both mandibles short and very broad, distinctly broader than in the closely related Apicotermes and Allognathotermes; fontanelle opening present but only punctiform and inconspicuous; labrum very small; sides of the head parallel; antennae 15-segmented; fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 apical spurs each; no pulvillus between the tarsal claws; fore coxa with a large, conspicuous tooth-like process. Type species Jugositermes tuberculatus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish yellow-brown, the anterior part darker, a dark longitudinal line running from the middle of the head to the rear; head rectangular, sides parallel, posterior margin rounded; the two ridges above the antennal bases distinct, the lower ridge weaker, the antennal bases set in a groove at one end; frons steeply inclined at about 45°; a small wart-like prominence on each side of the dorsal midline, visible in lateral view; setae on the head surface sparse, more numerous on both sides below the antennae; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 extremely short, shorter than segment 4, segment 4 shorter than segment 2; labrum very small, ligulate, inconspicuous; mandibles large and broad, proportionally short, the marginal teeth of both mandibles very short; fontanelle opening punctiform only, situated slightly anterior to the midline; margins of the pronotum with numerous long setae, the anterior margin with additional short hairs; pronotum narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, sides rather straight and narrowed posteriorly, posterior margin deeply concave with rounded angles, anterior margin concave, with a longitudinal groove in the middle; fore coxa with a large, conspicuous tooth-like process on the anterior side.

/species/kemneritermes-sarawakensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the genus-level key to soldiers of the Oriental Pericapritermes group, this is the only genus whose head has a highly sclerotised frontal ridge and is slightly phragmotic: couplet 1 separates it on this character alone, all the other genera having no frontal ridge and not being phragmotic.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head has a highly sclerotised frontal ridge and is slightly phragmotic.

/species/krecekitermes-daironi/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: One of the Neotropical Apicotermitinae with dehiscent organs, a structure shared with Dissimulitermes and Ruptitermes. It differs from Dissimulitermes in the trilobed enteric valve seat (EVS) (tubular in the latter) and in the enteric valve armature consisting of spines only, without sclerotised plates (the latter has sclerotised plates). It differs from Ruptitermes in having an armed enteric valve (unarmed in the latter, except R. bandeirai, a species far larger than this genus and with spines confined to 3 pads). The genus key gives the combination 'enteric valve seat trilobed, fewer than 13 spines on the armed pads'. The dehiscent organs fill the haemocoel in front of the crop; the midgut–P1 junction is clear, but the mixed segment is short.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dorsal surface of the head capsule concave in profile; fontanelle very distinct; postclypeus scarcely inflated, its median suture clear; antennal segments 14 or 15 (segment pattern 2>3<4≈5<6).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly concave in profile; antennae pale, with 13 or 14 segments (2>3<4<5); postclypeus strongly inflated. Left inner mandible: apical tooth as projecting as M1+2, the margin of M3 forming an obtuse angle, its tip truncate and directed backwards, the molar prominence well developed and projecting, completely concealing the molar lobe process in dorsal view; right inner mandible: apical tooth more projecting than M1, M1 well developed, M2 rounded at the tip, projecting and directed backwards, with an obtuse angle between M1 and M2. Dehiscent organs conspicuous in most individuals. Gut: mixed segment short, the midgut thickened at the tongue; enteric valve armature of 6 pads with sclerotised, crown-like distal ends bearing spines, situated on the posterior part of the pads.

/species/leptomyxotermes-doriae/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands erected this genus for the African forest species doriae, which had previously been placed in Coarctotermes together with Rhadinotermes. The alate has a distinct notch in the cutting edge before marginal tooth 3 of the left mandible, a feature shared with Rhadinotermes and Fulleritermes; but the compound eye and ocellus of this genus are very large and projecting, the fontanelle is slit-like and does not branch distinctly anteriorly, and the molar plate of the right mandible has only 6–7 ridges (7–9 in Fulleritermes, 13–14 in Grallatotermes). The soldier is monotypic with traces of dimorphism, the nasus cylindrical, the head strongly constricted behind the antennae, with 14 antennal segments.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical tooth of the left mandible is as long as marginal tooth 1, the distance from the apical tooth to marginal tooth 1 is half the distance between marginal teeth 1 and 3 (left mandible index about 50); the cutting edge between marginal teeth 1 and 3 has a distinct depression in front of marginal tooth 3. The apical tooth of the right mandible is nearly as long as marginal tooth 1, the posterior cutting edge of marginal tooth 1 about as long as that of marginal tooth 2, the latter distinctly concave; the surface of the molar plate has a notch near the base of the anterior margin, the posterior margin extended into a rounded wing, the first molar ridge tooth-like, the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base. Fontanelle slit-like, not branching distinctly anteriorly. Compound eye and ocellus very large and projecting.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic, with traces of dimorphism. Nasus cylindrical. Vestigial mandibles with a small point. Head capsule strongly constricted behind the antennae. Antennal segments 14.

/species/longustitermes-manni/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the worker the enteric valve seating (EVS) is trilobed, on which basis it is separated from Hirsutitermes, whose enteric valve seating is tubular; the armature of the enteric valve is a continuous garland-like structure covering the cuticle between the cushions and composed of several hundred minute, thin spines. It is smaller than Hirsutitermes.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The armature of the enteric valve (EVA) is a continuous garland-like structure, the spines small, thin and numbered in the hundreds, extending onto the cuticle between the cushions; the enteric valve seating is trilobed. The species is relatively small.

/species/macrosubulitermes-greavesi/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The left mandibular index of the alate is 1.07 (1.29–1.33 in Subulitermes microsoma); the soldier head is larger than in S. microsoma and broader and more globular posteriorly, the head length/head width ratio 1.49–1.71 (2.27 in S. microsoma).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The apical antennal segment is pale and the basal segments dark; the dark part of the pronotum is the same colour as the head (the pronotum of S. microsoma is paler); the tibiae and the ends of the femora are darker than the middle of the femora; the wings are darker than in S. microsoma (the punctures are denser); the sternites have dark patches at the sides and a pale middle; the vertex is gently raised between the ocelli; the profile of the head is strongly arched, with the highest point above the ocelli; the fontanelle is a pale narrow slit, forked at its front end and shorter than the ocelli; there are 15 antennal segments, segment 3 slightly longer than segments 2 and 4 and more globular at its end; the length of the postclypeus is less than half its width (0.20–0.22 × 0.47 mm); the left mandibular index is 1.07; the lateral margins of the pronotum converge posteriorly; tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: There are 8 setae on the base of the nasus and the vertex; the frontal projection and the head bear sparse short hairs; the hairs of the abdominal tergites are relatively dense and only slightly shorter than the marginal setae; the head is larger than in S. microsoma and broader and more globular posteriorly; the head length/head width ratio is 1.49–1.63 (perlevis) or 1.71 (greavesi); the head is very slightly constricted, with lateral swellings behind the base of the nasus; the frontal projection is nearly cylindrical; there are 12 antennal segments (perlevis), segments 2, 3 and 4 nearly equal in length; the mandibles have no apical point; the fore tibia is nearly as wide as the femur and slightly swollen; the abdomen is thick, broad and rounded.

/species/malagasitermes-milloti/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The left mandibular index is 0.66 (worker); it is closest to the Oriental Leucopitermes rather than to the African genera of the same branch (the smallest left mandibular index among the African genera being 1.12 in Eutermellus).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The frontal projection and vertex bear short hairs, with few hairs at the base of the nasus; there are a few setae on the vertex; the hairs of the abdominal tergites and sternites are long and dense, and the posterior margin of each plate bears a row of setae about twice as long as the body hairs; the head is markedly constricted and nearly globular posteriorly; the frontal projection is conical; there are 12–13 antennal segments; the right mandible has a short, sharp apical point and the left has none; the angle between the anterior and posterior parts of the pronotal profile is less than a right angle.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical teeth of both mandibles are relatively large compared with marginal tooth 1; the cutting edge of marginal teeth 1+2 of the left mandible is wavy; a distinct notch remains in front of marginal tooth 3 of the left mandible; marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible is slightly rounded; the left mandibular index is 0.66.

/species/mangolditermes-curveileum/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve is unarmed (as in Hydrecotermes and Rustitermes), but the extremely long, S-shaped P1 in left view distinguishes it from those two. Compared with Aparatermes: the midgut tongue is elongate (short in the latter), the pointed scales lie on the proximal part of the pads (mid-pad in the latter), and the fore tibia is relatively inflated. Compared with Anoplotermes, which likewise has an unarmed enteric valve: there is no white globular midgut nodule in ventral view of the midgut tongue, and the pads are trapezoidal and truncate at the base (spatulate in the latter). Compared with Disjunctitermes: the body is larger (maximum head width >0.75 mm, <0.7 mm in the latter), the pads are broader (narrow and slender in the latter), and the scales are clear only from the middle to the anterior part (over the whole pad in the latter). Compared with Tonsuritermes: the worker fontanelle is not especially prominent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Fontanelle oval, with indistinct boundaries; dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly concave in profile; antennae pale, with 14 segments (2<3≅4<5). Apical tooth of the left inner mandible more projecting than M1+2, forming an angle of 75° with M1+2, the posterior margin of M1+2 nearly straight and long; molar lobe process very acute, conspicuous in dorsal view, nearly as long as M3; molar prominence small. Apical tooth of the right inner mandible much more projecting than M1, the tip of M1 very acute, M2 forming an angle of almost 90° and directed backwards, with a shallow incision between M1 and M2 forming a broad, slightly obtuse angle; molar plate reduced and concave. Gut: crop small; the midgut tongue of the mixed segment long but not inflated; P1 extremely long in left view, curving in an S from one side of the crop to P3; enteric valve seat weakly trilobed; enteric valve unarmed, composed of 6 slender, inflated pads, the distal half of each bearing clear fringed pentagonal scales, the proximal end of each pad with about 10–20 minute triangular spines.

/species/mastotermes-darwiniensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Genus-level characters of the wing venation: the radial sector of the forewing is highly fused, with narrow spacing between adjacent upper branches; the humeral suture of the forewing is more curved and convex than in Blattotermes; the hindwing has a well-developed anal lobe, which the original describes as a character of this genus and its close relatives; the radial sector is compact and the media lies closer to the radial sector than to the anterior cubitus, which allows specimens known only from wings to be assigned to this genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Radial sector of the forewing highly fused, with narrow spacing between adjacent upper branches; the humeral suture of the forewing forms a distinct arcuate convexity and is more curved than in Blattotermes; the anal lobe of the hindwing is well developed.

/species/mycterotermes-meringocephalus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands erected this genus for meringocephalus, considering it close to Trinervitermes but more primitive and possibly even ancestral to it, with many diagnostic features in common with the Neotropical Diversitermes. Soldier dimorphic: the major soldier has a short, cylindrical nasus and the head capsule is very weakly constricted behind the antennae; the minor soldier has a weakly conical nasus and a more distinctly constricted head capsule; the major soldier possibly has 13 antennal segments and the minor soldier 12. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: nasus short, cylindrical, the vestigial mandibles with a small but distinct point showing traces of marginal and apical teeth; head capsule very weakly constricted behind the antennae, the vertex and nasus with short, distinct seta-like hairs. Minor soldier: identical to the major soldier except for the weakly conical nasus and the more distinctly constricted head capsule behind the antennae. Antennal segments possibly 13 in the major soldier and 12 in the minor soldier.

/species/ngauratermes-arue/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A genus living in the leaf litter of Amazonia, its name taken from the Ticuna word ngau'ra (leaf litter). Both the soldier and the worker are dimorphic; the alate is still unknown. The original author points out that the genus has many similarities with the group formed by Tenuirostritermes, Diversitermes and Velocitermes, being especially close to the last two.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. The mandibles have a distinct tooth-like projection; there are 13 antennal segments; the base of the nasus is narrow and nearly cylindrical. The head capsule of the major soldier is broad, slightly constricted behind the antennae and narrowed anteriorly at the sides; that of the minor soldier is narrow and elongate, with a marked constriction behind the antennae. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic, divided into a narrow-gap and a wide-gap form; the two forms overlap in size and cannot be separated as major and minor workers; the wide-gap form is rare, 6 of 103 workers in the type series, with a left mandibular index of 0.32. The worker has 14 antennal segments, segment 4 very short and unsclerotised; the left mandibular index is 0.35; the molar plate is broad, concave and weakly ridged. P1 is a simple tube without an apical ring; the enteric valve is conical and curved, situated posteriorly and inserted into P3 from the upper left side, weakly sclerotised and with two rings of spines.

/species/noirotitermes-noiroti/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the posterior part of the head bears four conspicuous horn-like projections, the sides are convex and the anterior half is slightly constricted; the shape of the head capsule is highly distinctive and the head surface bears a characteristic micro-sculpture; the mandibles are of the piercing type; the species is relatively small. In the alate the left mandibular index is 1.5, the antennae have 15 segments and the segment order is 1>2>6>5=4>3.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The posterior part of the head bears four conspicuous horn-like projections, the sides are convex and the anterior half is slightly constricted; the shape of the head capsule is highly distinctive and the head surface bears a characteristic micro-sculpture; the mandibles are of the piercing type; the species is smaller than its congeners.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is brown with a semicircular pale patch on the frons, the fontanelle spot elliptical and also pale, and the ecdysial line pale. The postclypeus is distinctly inflated, with a straight anterior margin, a convex posterior margin and a distinct median line. The compound eyes are circular and medium-sized; the ocelli are large and distinct. The apical tooth of the mandibles is large, and M3 of the left mandible is far shorter than M1; the left mandibular index is 1.5. There are 15 antennal segments, their order 1>2>6>5=4>3. The micro-sculpture of the wing surface is almost absent, fine points occurring only near the base of the anterior part.

/species/oriencapritermes-kluangensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It shares couplet 13 with Syncapritermes: this genus has the anterior margin of the labrum deeply concave, the labrum about as long as wide, and the anterolateral projections with a point at their base, whereas Syncapritermes has the anterior margin shallowly concave, the labrum longer than wide, and the base of the anterolateral projections without a point. The left mandible has a well-developed, toothed inferior basal process (couplet 12).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The anterior margin of the labrum is deeply concave, the labrum about as long as wide and the base of the anterolateral projections pointed; the left mandible has a well-developed, toothed inferior basal process; the labrum is long (length ≥ width); the fontanelle is small and circular, and the fontanelle gland small; the middle of the left mandible is strongly twisted and its tip blunt.

/species/ourissotermes-giblinorum/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve armature consists of 6 groups of pectinate spine bundles, each with 4–6 rows of spines: longer spines distally near P3, decreasing posteriorly, together with smaller tooth-like spines; the proximal end of each pad (near P1) bears 1 small tooth-like spine; the enteric valve is inserted directly into P3 without a differentiated enteric valve seat (EVS). On this basis it is distinguished from Patawatermes (enteric valve seat drawn out into a tube, clearly visible externally) and Echinotermes (enteric valve seat trilobed). The external gut morphology resembles Hydrecotermes, but the enteric valve of the latter is unarmed. The generic name refers to the sea-urchin-like appearance of the enteric valve armature (Portuguese ouriço).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head slightly concave above the ocelli; fontanelle very small or indistinct; compound eye and ocellus nearly round; antennal segments 15 (segment pattern 2>3<4<5<6); lateral margins of the pronotum elongate and smoothly rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Anterior part of the dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly convex in profile; postclypeus strongly inflated; antennal segments 14. Apical tooth of the left inner mandible more projecting than M1+2, the margin of M3 forming an obtuse-angled triangle with a slightly truncate tip, the molar prominence well developed, partly concealing the molar lobe process; apical tooth of the right inner mandible more projecting than M1, M2 triangular with an acute angle, its tip projecting but slightly less than M1. Gut: midgut tongue small, P1 joined to the midgut by a simple transverse connection; enteric valve seat indistinct; enteric valve armature as in the genus diagnosis (6 groups of pectinate spine bundles, the distal spines long and decreasing posteriorly).

/species/paracurvitermes-manni/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the soldier the body is relatively small; the head capsule is relatively wide, circular or nearly square, its base about as long as wide; the frontal tube is well developed, conical and relatively short; the mandibles are of the piercing type and distinctly curved, being longer and less curved than in Acangaobitermes, with triangular teeth and a conspicuous marginal tooth near the base. In the alate the left mandibular index is about 2.0.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head capsule is relatively wide, circular or nearly square, its base about as long as wide. The frontal tube is well developed and conical, shorter than in Biratermes. The mandibles are of the piercing type and distinctly curved; they are longer and less curved than in Acangaobitermes, with triangular teeth, and bear a conspicuous marginal tooth near the base.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The left mandibular index is about 2.0, as in Curvitermes and Cyrilliotermes.

/species/paraneotermes-simplicicornis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate has a distinct obtuse flexure on the posterior margins of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible, and the arolium is absent; the soldier mandibles are relatively short for the head length and stout, which distinguishes it from Comatermes and Ceratokalotermes (see their respective entries).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark smoky brown; eye small, about 0.28 mm in diameter, the ocellus about 0.02 mm from the compound eye; antennal segments 14–15; marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible broader at the base than marginal tooth 3, their posterior margins slightly longer than the anterior margin of marginal tooth 3, with an obtuse flexure about 1/4 from the tip; the molar plate of the right mandible nearly as long as the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2; pronotum slightly broader than the head, the anterior margin broadly and shallowly concave; radial sector with 6–7 branches; media paler than the radial sector and weakly sclerotised; arolium absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head long, flattened dorsoventrally; frons slightly concave along the mid-line, sloping down to the clypeus at about 35°; eye colourless; antennal segments 13–15, the third as long as the second; mandibles relatively short for the head length and stout, with a basal boss; anterior part of the postmentum very broad; pronotum as broad as the head, the anterior margin broadly concave; femora distinctly inflated.

/species/postsubulitermes-parviconstrict.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Erected by Emerson (1960) and supplemented by Sands (1965): soldier monotypic, the nasus slenderly cylindrical, tapering forwards to a fine point, the mandibles without a point, the anterior margin of the labrum evenly rounded, the head capsule hardly constricted behind the antennal sockets, the base of the nasus slightly raised, antennal segments 12, setae extremely few (one pair on the vertex, 1–2 pairs at the base of the nasus, a few at the nasus tip); alate postclypeus moderately inflated, twice as wide as long, the anterior margin undulate with a median convexity, fontanelle long and Y-shaped, compound eyes not projecting beyond the sides of the head, pilosity extremely fine and sparse (3 hairs on each eye, 2 pairs on the vertex, 1 pair on the postclypeus), the lateral margins of the pronotum contracted posteriorly, the length less than two-thirds of the width; worker apical tooth of the left mandible much longer than marginal tooth 1 (index 2.63), the cutting edge between marginal teeth 1–3 entire and concave, the gap between marginal tooth 3 and the molar prominence extremely narrow, marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible absent, the molar plate weakly concave near the base, with a weak anterior and a strong rounded posterior ridge, without transverse ridges. Emerson's supplement: head dark brown and pronotum yellow, strongly contrasting; soldier head length 1.39–1.53 mm, width 0.55–0.60 mm, pronotum 0.34–0.39 mm, hind tibia 0.71–0.79 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and postclypeus with sparse short hairs and several long setae; the pronotum has many long setae near the lateral and posterior margins and a few short hairs on the surface; the abdominal tergites and sternites both bear many long setae or hairs of nearly equal length. Ocelli large and distinct, less than half their own width from the compound eye, slightly larger than the antennal socket. Fontanelle pale brown, elongate, furcate at the tip, situated in a shallow depression on the vertex. Postclypeus about half as long as wide (0.18 mm × 0.36 mm). The lateral margins of the pronotum rather straight and contracted posteriorly, the posterior angles rounded, the posterior margin slightly concave; the posterior angles of the mesonotum slightly less than right angles, the median emargination slightly greater than a right angle; the posterior angles of the metanotum more rounded, about equal to a right angle, the median emargination angle greater than that of the mesonotum. Spur formula 2:2:2. The antennae of the specimens are broken off.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head surface scattered with setae and short hairs; the tip of the frontal projection bears several hairs, but the middle and base of the frontal projection are without short hairs. Pronotum with a few short hairs, more numerous anteriorly. Each abdominal tergite with a row of posterior marginal setae and scattered hairs about one-third their length; the setae and hairs of the sternites are longer than those of the tergites, the hairs about half the length of the setae. Head oval in dorsal view, the frontal projection slender and elongate, tapering slightly forwards, a slight constriction visible behind the antennal sockets (in both dorsal and lateral view). Antennal segments 12. Mandibles without a point. Anterior margin of the pronotum very shallowly and indistinctly concave. Spur formula 2:2:2. Head dark brown, pronotum yellow, strongly contrasting.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The apical tooth of the mandible is proportionally longer than in Afrosubulitermes and Verrucositermes; marginal tooth 3 of the left mandible is indistinct, the cutting edge between marginal teeth 1 and 3 entire and concave, the gap between marginal tooth 3 and the molar prominence extremely narrow; marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible is absent, the molar plate weakly concave near the base, with a weak anterior ridge and a strong rounded posterior ridge, without transverse ridges. Left mandible index 2.63.

/species/profastigitermes-putnami/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
