sections.text: Above and slightly behind the opening of the fontanelle the vertex forms a rounded hump (the hump of Fastigitermes extends further forwards); the postmentum narrows from below and at its narrowest is a conspicuous double-pointed projection, whereas the corresponding projection of Fastigitermes is a single, sharp backward-pointing spine.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The surface of the head bears scattered setae, and a large tuft of long hairs surrounds the opening of the fontanelle; there are a few setae near the anterior margin of the labrum and on the anterior margin of the postmentum; the postmentum narrows from below, with a double-pointed projection situated about one quarter of the way in front of the middle of its posterior margin, between whose two points a slightly concave ridge is visible in anterior view.

/species/protohamitermes-globiceps/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus, containing only globiceps, from Sarawak, Borneo. The left mandible has a Leucotermes-type dentition (4 teeth before the basal tooth), on which basis Holmgren placed the genus in the Hamitermes branch and considered it fairly primitive within that branch. The alate is brown, thickly haired, with fairly short, hairy wings and 14 antennal segments; the worker has 13 antennal segments. The soldier is unknown.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brown, thickly haired, the wings fairly short and hairy. The head is very broadly convex, slightly depressed around the frontal gland pore. The compound eyes are medium-sized and fairly strongly convex; the ocelli are relatively small and more than one eye diameter from the compound eyes. The frontal gland pore lies behind the middle of the head; it is large and dark. The base of the clypeus is very short and flat, without a longitudinal line, and the apex is large. The left mandible has a Leucotermes-type dentition with 4 teeth before the basal tooth; the right mandible has only 3 anterior teeth, of which the apical tooth is far shorter than the others. There are 14 antennal segments, segment 3 small. The pronotum is narrower than the head; the posterior emargination of the mesonotum is wider than that of the metanotum. The forewing scale is slightly larger than the hindwing scale; the media has 1–2 apical branches and the cubitus 12–18; all the veins are distinct, and the inner 5–7 are thickened. The cerci are thick and short; there are no styli; the tarsi are short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The pilosity is dense and setose. The head is circular, sometimes even wider than long, thick, and slightly depressed in the middle. The frontal gland pore is large, sometimes dark. The base of the clypeus is short and flat. The mandibular base is large, and the mandibles are as in the alate. There are 13 antennal segments, fairly thick, segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and segment 4 longer than segment 3. The pronotum is short and saddle-shaped, its anterior margin not emarginate. The cerci are short and thick; there are no styli. The tarsi are short. The abdomen is thick.

/species/pseudomicrotermes-alboniger/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A new genus established by Holmgren 1912 with a single species, Pseudomicrotermes alboniger (Wasm.), from Congo; a synonym in part is Mirotermes (Wasmann 1911). It was formerly placed in Microtermes and was separated because morphological examination showed its similarity to Microtermes to be merely one of habit; according to Holmgren's comparison table the alate of this genus is 'very small' with a very large head, far wider than the pronotum, and the soldier head is rectangular and far longer than wide, differing from Microtermes in the length of the clypeal base, the length/width ratio of the labrum, the mandibular dentition and the wing venation (presence or absence of an accessory vein and of a reticulation). The soldier labrum is lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide; the mandibles are blade-like and curved, not concave on the outer margin at the base; there are 13–14 antennal segments; the cerci are unusually long; there are no styli.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very small. The head is very large, fairly strongly raised, thick and slightly narrowed anteriorly. The compound eyes are medium-sized and flat. The ocelli are small, almost no more than their own diameter from the compound eyes, directed fully laterally, their inner margins slightly raised. The frontal gland pore is far back, with a dark spot in the middle. The transverse band is very long. The base of the clypeus is short, far less than half its width and slightly raised, its posterior margin slightly concave and its anterior margin straight. The labrum is about as wide as long. The apical tooth of the mandibles is slightly swollen. There are 16 antennal segments, thickening towards the apex. The pronotum is fairly small, its anterior lobe incurved and its anterior margin concave; the posterior margin is concave. The posterior parts of the meso- and metanota are slightly pointed and rectangularly emarginate. The forewing scale is slightly larger than the hindwing scale. The wing membrane is transparent with very fine spine-like points and without a reticulation; the veins are very indistinct; the media lies close to the cubitus and appears to branch only very weakly (simple?); there are about 10 cubital veins. The abdomen is white. The fore tibia bears 3 apical spurs, the mid and hind tibiae only 2 each. The penultimate tarsomere is extended into a slender projection. The cerci are fairly long. There are no styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is rectangular with rounded corners, far longer than wide, and thick. The frons is slightly inclined. The frontal gland pore lies on the horizontal part of the head, near the edge of the inclined part. The labrum is lanceolate, more than twice as long as wide, with a small transparent apex behind which a few setae arise. The mandibles are blade-like and curved, not concave on the outer margin at the base. The left mandible has one or two lobed basal teeth and three very small but sharp teeth in the middle; the apex is weak and minutely saw-like. The base of the right mandible has two small teeth, and its middle bears only a tooth-like blunt dilation. There are 13–14 antennal segments, thickening towards the apex. The pronotum is small and saddle-shaped, with a large anterior lobe and a deeply concave anterior margin. The cerci are unusually long. There are no styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head is broadly oval, longer than wide. The frontal gland pore is fairly far back. The base of the clypeus is slightly shorter than half its width, its posterior margin fairly strongly convex and its anterior margin slightly concave. The mandibles are as in the alate. There are 15–16 antennal segments. The pronotum is saddle-shaped with a deeply concave anterior margin. The cerci are long. There are no styli.

/species/pterotermes-occidentis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is closely related to Incisitermes and Marginitermes but differs in the large eye (0.68–0.71 mm in diameter) and 20–21 antennal segments; the soldier is the largest in the family, with pigmented eyes, a nearly saddle-shaped pronotum and a sclerotised swelling at the base of the postmentum.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Brown; eye large, 0.68–0.71 mm in diameter, the ocellus touching the compound eye; antennal segments 20–21; the bases of marginal teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible as long as marginal tooth 3, their posterior margins as long as the anterior margin of marginal tooth 3; the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible as long as the molar plate; pronotum as broad as the head; subcosta of the forewing long, unbranched; radial sector with 5–6 branches, the first at about 1/4 of the wing length; media weak, unsclerotised, lying between the radial sector and the cubitus, branched distally in some specimens; arolium always absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Largest in the family; head very large, the sides rounded; frons sloping gradually forwards from about the middle of the head; postclypeus with one median ridge on each side, as in Rugitermes; a horn-like projection below and in front of the antennal socket, near the lateral base of the mandibles; eye pigmented; antennal segments 17, the third longer than the second and fourth; mandibles long and thick, toothed, with a distinct basal boss; postmentum with a sclerotised swelling at the base; pronotum broader than the head, somewhat saddle-shaped, the anterior margin deeply concave and covering the back of the head, the anterolateral corners raised; meso- and metathorax with distinct wing buds; femora inflated.

/species/quasitermes-incisus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The labrum is almost asymmetrical, its lateral points short and sharp; the labrum of Mirocapritermes is more asymmetrical and more deeply forked, with longer and sharper lateral points (Emerson 1950).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is elongate and nearly square, its sides parallel and slightly convex; the frontal projection points forwards and is not very sharp (the quotation is interrupted here by the original running head with the page number); the labrum is longer than wide, its apex shallowly concave or angulate; the mandibles are asymmetrical and suited to snapping, the left slightly wavy and the right slightly curved outwards.

/species/rhadinotermes-coarctatus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Sands placed this genus in the Procornitermes branch; the soldier head capsule is sharply constricted behind the antennal sockets, similar to Fulleritermes, but it is not phylogenetically close to Leptomyxotermes/Grallatotermes, belonging instead to a mainly Neotropical clade containing Velocitermes, Tenuirostritermes and Diversitermes; the former placement in Coarctotermes was based only on soldier similarity. Soldier monotypic, the nasus conical, the mandibles with a small point, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part, antennal segments 12; alate left mandible index 0.32–0.36, marginal tooth 2 absent, the molar plate of the right mandible with 6–7 transverse ridges diminishing towards the base, the first forming a stout tooth, the fontanelle an extremely narrow slit and hardly branching anteriorly. The genus name derives from the Greek rhadinos (tapering).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule very dark brown to pitch black, postclypeus and antennae dark sepia-brown, wings semi-transparent pale brown; the posterior margin of the head behind the compound eyes is almost semicircular; compound eyes not projecting, relatively small for the head (W/E 3.4–3.8), slightly angular-oval; ocelli small and oval, their distance from the compound eye about 1.5 times their own least diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, 2.2 times as wide as long, the anterior margin slightly concave; antennal segments 15, segments II, IV and V nearly equal in length, II more slender, III longer. Mandibles: the apical tooth of the left mandible equal to or slightly shorter than marginal tooth 1, the distance from the apical tooth to marginal tooth 1 about one-third of the distance between marginal teeth 1 and 3 (index 0.32–0.36), marginal tooth 2 absent, the cutting edge between marginal teeth 1 and 3 entire; the apical tooth of the right mandible nearly equal to marginal tooth 1, marginal tooth 1 with a small accessory tooth near its tip; the molar plate of the right mandible weakly concave near the base of the anterior margin, the posterior margin extended into a rounded ridge, the first transverse ridge forming a stout tooth, the remaining 6–7 diminishing towards the base; fontanelle extremely narrow, slit-like, hardly branching anteriorly (more pronounced in females), slightly paler than the head to distinctly pale.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Nasus conical. Mandibles vestigial, with a small point. Head capsule sharply constricted behind the antennal sockets, the posterior lobe usually only about a quarter wider than the anterior part. Antennal segments 12. Head capsule sepia-brown to pitch black, the nasus black with a reddish tip; the lateral profile of the head is raised and rounded behind the constriction and rather straight in front of it; the nasus is as long as or shorter than the rest of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal sockets; nasus cone angle 10–20°; antennal segment II short, IV and V longer; setae confined to 4 at the nasus tip, one pair on the vertex and a few short curved hairs on the dorsal surface. 25 specimens: head length (to the nasus tip) 1.17–1.39 mm, head width 0.54–0.66 mm, hind tibia 0.92–1.10 mm.

/species/roisinitermes-ebogoensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The only genus in the Kalotermitidae with snapping mandibles: the soldier mandibles are slender rods with a very weak dentition; the alate has no visible ocelli, also unique in the family. In Krishna's (1961) generic key the alate runs to couplet 2 (Epicalotermes) and the soldier to couplet 17 (Allotermes). The soldier mandibles somewhat resemble the slender, nearly edentate mandibles of Allotermes (especially A. denticulatus), but in this genus the mandibles curve downwards in lateral view, which is unique among kalotermitids with projecting mandibles; although the alate wing venation and dentition are very close to those of Epicalotermes, the soldier shares no major character with that genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and pronotum pale brownish orange, the abdominal tergites paler, concolorous with the legs and labrum; postclypeus almost transparent. Compound eyes medium-sized and projecting, oval, truncate near the antennal socket, composed of about 85 ommatidia; ocelli neither pigmented nor with a cuticular prominence, entirely invisible. Antennal segments more than 9, the segment pattern 1>2=3=4<5 (14–17 segments recorded at species level). Pronotum about twice as wide as its median length, the lateral margins with several long setae and shorter setae. Forewing M and Cu stalked beyond the scale suture, the radial sector (Rs) with 5–6 anterior branches, the subcosta (Sc) closely applied to the anterior margin and difficult to distinguish; hindwing Rs and Cu stalked behind the suture. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi without an arolium. The anterior margin of the marginal tooth of the left mandible is about 1.5 times the combined length of its posterior margin and the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2; the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2 of the right mandible is 1.4 times the length of the molar plate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Eye spot distinct, large and dark brown. Frons bilobed in dorsal view, covered with wrinkled longitudinal ridges, the ridges below the frons arranged longitudinally; the ventral cheeks end in a small angular projection. Mandibles slender rods, curved downwards in lateral view; dentition very weak, the basal swelling sharply projecting forwards.

/species/roonwalitermes-wadhwai/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus endemic to north-eastern India. Soldier dimorphic: major soldier with the head capsule globular, not constricted behind the antennae, abruptly narrowed anteriorly into a long, narrow cylindrical nasus (almost as long as the head), antennae 13-segmented; minor soldier with the head pyriform, antennae 11–12-segmented. Worker antennae 13-segmented, postclypeus only slightly raised (about one-quarter as long as wide).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major soldier: head capsule globular, not constricted behind the antennae, densely covered with fine hairs; anterior part abruptly narrowed into a long, narrow, cylindrical nasus almost as long as the head; in lateral view the head capsule is slightly incurved at the base of the nasus; antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 long, narrow, club-shaped, segment 4 shortest; mandibles vestigial, each with a short spine-like process and without teeth; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped; legs slender, tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Minor soldier: head pyriform, not constricted behind the antennae; anterior part narrowed into a long, narrow nasus, with a weak swelling at the base of the nasus in lateral view; antennae 11–12-segmented; mandibles vestigial, with short spines; pronotum and legs as in the major soldier.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head subcircular; frontal gland pore circular; coronal suture present; antennae 13-segmented, the segments short and broadly rounded; postclypeus weakly raised, about one-quarter as long as wide; mandibles with an apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth and marginal tooth 1 subequal in length, the angle between them narrow; left mandible with the posterior margin of marginal tooth 1 long and straight, marginal tooth 2 short and triangular, the margin between marginal tooth 2 and the molar plate strongly incurved, the molar prominence small and pointed; right mandible with the posterior margin of marginal tooth 1 longer than the anterior margin, marginal tooth 2 short with a long, straight posterior margin, the molar plate about 1.25 times the posterior margin of marginal tooth 2; pronotum and legs as in the soldier.

/species/rounditermes-dechambrei/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distinguished from the closely related Cortaritermes: soldier antennae constantly with 14 segments, the head capsule longer and wider, the hind tibia relatively longer, the head surface lacking microtrichia, the nasus more conical and shorter. The original twice emphasises that the head capsule is round, as long as wide, and not constricted behind the level of the antennal sockets, by which it can be distinguished from the species of Cortaritermes, which have a narrower head capsule and a more slender nasus; the genus name is taken from the roundness of the soldier head capsule.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (1) head dark brown, round, as long as wide, not constricted behind the level of the antennae; (2) nasus conical, slightly upturned; (3) head surface with a few long hairs, mainly around the base of the nasus; (4) 4–5 long hairs and several small hairs at the nasus tip, a few hairs at the base; (5) mandibles slender, small, vestigial, but with a distinct sharp point; (6) antennae nearly concolorous with the head, constantly 14 segments; segment 1 longer than the rest, segment 2 shorter than the rest, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 5, segments 3 and 4 about equal; (7) pronotum pale brown, the anterior margin raised and with an emargination, about 7 long erect setae, a few fine hairs behind; the pronotum broadly rounded anteriorly and posteriorly, concave in the middle, depressed laterally; (8) abdominal tergites yellowish brown, with several hairs on the posterior margins; (9) sternites yellow, with many long hairs on the posterior margins; (10) legs yellow, slender, the tibiae and femora with rows of long hairs and spines; (11) means of 10 specimens: body length 5.20 mm, head length including nasus 1.99 mm, head width 1.55 mm, nasus length 0.72 mm, pronotum length 0.40 mm, antennal length 1.97 mm, hind tibia 1.77 mm, hind tibia about 0.9 times the head length.

/species/rubeotermes-jheringi/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker turns red in alcohol and the fore coxa bears several long, thick spines as large as the tarsal spur, characters by which it can be distinguished from all South American soldierless termites.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes and ocelli medium-sized. Fontanelle very small. Pronotum semicircular in dorsal view, with several hundred setae. The posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum are rather concave, the angles rounded.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large, head width about 1 mm. White in life, turning red in alcohol. Head capsule densely covered with many small setae; fontanelle very small. Fore coxa with several spines as large as the tarsal spur; fore tibia slightly inflated. The junction of the midgut and proctodeum is truncate, without a mixed segment (the original reads 'Mesenteron and proctodeum connection truncated, devoid of mixed segment'); the enteric valve inserts into a trilobed enteric valve seating.

/species/rustitermes-boteroi/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve has 6 slightly asymmetrical pads, each forming a central pouch whose scales are smaller than those between the pads; each pad bears about 60–80 scales, broad at the base and narrow at the tip; the posterior part of each pad is truncate and bears 35–50 rectangular scales arranged from the middle towards the tip and becoming denser distally. It differs from Hydrecotermes, which has a similar gut coiling, in the worker fore tibia bearing coarse setae on the inner margin (absent in the latter). It differs from Aparatermes, whose enteric valve and gut may be similar, in the cuticle between the pads bearing cubical scales (absent in the latter); the enteric valve seat is not trilobed (trilobed in the latter); the enteric valve has no spinules or acute scales (present in the latter); and the posterior part of the pads bears scales (no scales posteriorly in the latter).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The fontanelle is indistinct in both sexes, the fontanellar region depressed, the median spot faintly visible. Apical tooth of the left inner mandible slightly larger than M1+2, M3 triangular with an obtuse lateral angle, the anterior molar process indistinct, the molar lobe process not concealed by the molar prominence. Head capsule dark brown with short, sparse setae; the frontal markings slightly paler than the rest of the head capsule, with indistinct boundaries. Pronotum nearly hexagonal, the anterior margin straight without a median notch, the lateral margins very straight and distinct, the surface sparsely covered with setae and short hairs. Tergites and sternites with short hairs. Fore coxa with 4–5 conspicuous long setae; the inner face of the fore tibia with 2 rows of 6–7 coarse setae each.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; fontanelle small and round; postclypeus slightly inflated; head capsule with medium and long setae. Apical tooth of the left inner mandible more projecting than M1+2, M3 triangular with a right or acute lateral angle, the molar lobe process not concealed by the molar prominence. Long pronotal setae concentrated along the margins of the anterior and posterior lobes; tergites and sternites densely covered with long setae, mostly directed backwards or upwards. Fore coxa with 4–5 coarse setae; the inner face of the fore femur with long setae; fore tibia moderately inflated, the inner face with 2 rows of 6–7 coarse setae each. Enteric valve unarmed, with 6 pyriform pads of slightly different sizes, composed of larger fringed polygonal scales; the cuticle between the pads consists of still larger fringed cubical scales, densely arranged near P3.

/species/sandsitermes-robustus/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The dorsal surface of the alate head is slightly raised anterior to the fontanelle at the position of the ocelli; the postclypeus is slightly arched, with a straight anterior margin and a slightly convex posterior margin; the molar region of the right mandible is distinctly concave, with weak ridges and a distinct basal concavity. The soldier nasus is long-conical but has no unique morphological character (the original explicitly states 'no apparent uniquely distinct morphological character'). The worker mandible has a concave molar region without well-developed ridges; P1 of the gut forms a separate loop before joining the paunch (P3); the enteric valve (P2) is weakly sclerotised, arranged in two rings, with minute conical spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule oval in dorsal view; the frontal region between the ocelli is not concave; in lateral view the dorsal surface of the head is slightly raised anterior to the fontanelle at the position of the ocelli. Compound eyes oval and large, closer to the lower margin of the head than to the ocelli. Ocelli elliptical and large in dorsal view (smaller than the antennal socket), situated in the anterior half of the compound eye, their distance from the compound eye less than the width of an ocellus. Fontanelle paler than the head, situated in a shallow depression, Y-shaped, the anterior arms short, with a small transparent circle above the arms. Postclypeus slightly arched in lateral view, slightly concave along the midline in dorsal view; anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly convex. Antennal segments 15. Pronotum wider than the head (excluding the eyes), sub-trapezoidal, the anterior margin raised, the anterolateral angles rounded, the lateral margins concave and narrowing posteriorly, the posterior margin rounded and not concave. The posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum deeply concave, the posterolateral angles acute. Spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule oval to round in dorsal view, not constricted, the posterior margin not concave; in lateral view the vertex is slightly raised at the base of the nasus, with a shallow depression behind it. Nasus conical, shorter than the head capsule, not upturned; postclypeus slightly convex in lateral view. Labrum wider than long, the anterior margin rounded, the lateral margins parallel, the anterior angles rounded. Mandibles with a distinct 'point'. Antennal segments 13. The anterior lobe of the pronotum is less developed than the posterior lobe, the angle between them about 90°. Fore coxa conical, without a keel on the anterior face. Spur formula 2:2:2. Abdominal sclerites well sclerotised, the tergites imbricate.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: All workers with a trapezoidal head capsule; fontanelle distinct, situated in the middle of the head capsule, slightly concave; postclypeus inflated; antennal segments 14; anterior margin of the pronotum rounded and not concave; spur formula 2:2:2. Workers dimorphic, distinguished by head capsule pigmentation, mandible form and the shape and size of the tergites: type 2 is less numerous than type 1 in all samples examined, the head capsule brownish yellow, with a concavity anteriorly and a swelling behind it; the outer margin of the mandible has a distinct concavity in front of the apical tooth, the apical tooth is larger, the gap between left M3 and the molar prominence is wider, and the molar plate is narrower; the anterior lobe of the pronotum is more developed than the posterior lobe. Within type 1 the head capsule size appears to vary, but the number of individuals is insufficient for measurement.

/species/scheffrahnitermes-ubuntu/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Monotypic genus (Scheffrahnitermes ubuntu), without soldiers (Apicotermitinae). The enteric valve seating (EVS) is unique: internally with two unequal sclerotised spiny plates (the spines directed towards P3), spines also present between the plates; externally forming a small pouch at the P1–P3 junction (the larger plate fitting precisely into the pouch); the body colour of the worker turns red after preservation in alcohol. Distinguished from Grigiotermes, Dissimulitermes and Humutermes: in the latter three the sclerotised plates lie within the enteric valve (EV), one in each of the six valves, whereas in this genus they lie within the enteric valve seating; distinguished from the closely related species of Ruptitermes: in the latter the enteric valve seating forms three small pouches, in this genus only one; it shares the ‘turning red in alcohol’ character with Rubeotermes and Tonsuritermes, but body shape, gut coiling and mixed segment differ, and this genus lacks spines on the fore tibia/fore coxa (Tonsuritermes has spines on the fore tibia, Rubeotermes on the fore coxa).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Female larger than male. Fontanelle conspicuous, subcircular, the medium-sized spot distinct; compound eyes circular, ocelli elliptical, the distance between the ocellus and the compound eye less than its diameter. Left mandible with the apical tooth equal in size to M1+2, M3 triangular with a sharp edge, a gap between M3 and the distinct premolar prominence; right mandible with the apical tooth subequal to M1, M2 triangular with a sharp edge. Head capsule rounded dorsally, densely covered with short hairs and short, medium and long setae; deep brown, paler around the antennae. Antennae 15-segmented (formula 2>3<4=5). Postclypeus slightly inflated, slightly paler than the head capsule, median suture distinct. Labrum covered with short hairs and setae. Pronotum sub-trapezoidal, shorter than the head, anterior margin straight with a median incision, median suture distinct, densely covered with hairs of different sizes and setae. Fore tibia long and slender, not inflated, with a few short, stout setae on the inner surface. Wings three times the length of the abdomen; veins brown, membrane transparent and slightly brownish; forewing and hindwing with short marginal cilia (except on the basal third of the posterior margin).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule and thorax change from pale yellow to deep red/brown after preservation in alcohol. Sides of the head slightly convex, dorsally rounded, with scattered setae and short to medium hairs. Postclypeus inflated, often with a pair of setae at the apex. Fontanelle large and conspicuous. Antennae 12–14-segmented (formula 2>3=4<5), pale at the base and becoming progressively darker towards the apex. Left mandible with the apical tooth equal in size to M1+2, M3 triangular with a sharp edge, a gap between M3 and the premolar prominence; right mandible with the apical tooth subequal to M1, M2 triangular with a sharp edge. Anterior lobe and posterior margin of the pronotum with long setae and short hairs. Fore tibia moderately inflated, with short hairs and 5–6 long, stout setae. Crop spherical, inflated when full; cardiac valve long, inserted at the anterior end of the midgut; a small white spherical nodule on the ventral side at the junction of the mixed segment and P1; P1 of uniform width, widened and folded, forming a mirrored C shape ventrally; enteric valve (EV) with six columnar pads, each pad with a short spine at its base and covered with small scales (the central ones sub-trapezoidal, the marginal ones subrectangular), the small spines on the scale margins directed towards P3; enteric valve seating (EVS) short, forming a small pouch, internally with two asymmetrical sclerotised plates, the spines directed towards P3, spines also present between the plates, the larger plate aligned with the pouch; P3 connected to P4 by an isthmus on the left side of the body; P4 turning in a U-shape after the mixed segment, its end entering the inflated P5 dorsally. Measurements (mm, n=30, six nests): head width 0.63–0.73 (0.68), head length 0.78–0.90 (0.83), fore tibia width 0.09–0.13 (0.11), fore tibia length 0.36–0.49 (0.45), tibial index 0.74–0.87 (0.82).

/species/schievitermes-globicornis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier differs from Termes, Inquilinitermes, Cavitermes, Palmitermes, Dihoplotermes and Cornicapritermes among the Neotropical snappers in lacking a frontal projection; Planicapritermes has a flattened head capsule and strongly asymmetrical mandibles; it differs from Crepititermes in the thicker mandibles with a slight but distinct asymmetry and the globular third antennal segment; the species of Neocapritermes are larger (head width >1 mm), have 15–16 antennal segments (13 in this genus), and their mandibles are always more strongly asymmetrical. The worker mandibles are of the wood-feeding type, with a short distance between the apical tooth and the first marginal tooth and well-developed molar ridges; the digestive tract resembles that of Planicapritermes, but the bilobed distal end of the mesenteric part of the mixed segment is characteristic of this genus; Neocapritermes also has two mesenteric lobes, but the mixed segment is shorter and the lobes are larger and more widely separated. The cuticular differentiation of P3 is intermediate between that of Neocapritermes (long spines and filaments) and Planicapritermes (minute spines).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The genus is known only from a single queen; the original did not give a separate genus-level description but referred to the species-level description. Nothing is added here.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head capsule is subquadrate with rounded corners, about 2 times as long as wide, and bears about 100 setae. The mandibles are about as long as the head capsule, relatively thick and of the snapping type; the right mandible is nearly straight, only slightly incurved; the left mandible is slightly but distinctly curved: the outer margin is slightly concave at the base, convex in the middle, concave again where it meets the right mandible, and incurved at the apex. The apices of both mandibles are hooked and turned inwards by about 60°. There are 13 antennal segments, the last extending beyond the apex of the left mandible; the third segment is distinctly globular, as wide as the first and wider than the remaining segments. The sides of the labrum are nearly parallel, the anterior margin is wavy and convex in the middle, with a few long setae, and the anterior corners are rounded. The frons has no projection.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. The head capsule is white and bears numerous setae. The mandibles are of the wood-feeding type: on the left mandible the distance A–M1+2 is about half the distance M1+2–M3; M3 is distinct, the premolar tooth (sensu Deligne 1999) is blade-like, and the molar ridges are well developed. On the right mandible the distance A–M1 is short, M2 is distinct, and the molar ridges are well developed. The crop is moderately developed; the gizzard is of the broad type, its cuticular armature being restricted to small comb-like scales on the pulvilli. The mixed segment is long, and the distal end of the mesenteric tongue is bilobed. P1 is slightly dilated and then narrows gradually into P2. The enteric valve (P2) is funnel-shaped, conical at the end of P1 and forming a narrow tube where it joins P3; the armature consists of two rings of spines: the proximal ring lies on the conical part of P2 and consists of 3 oval cushions alternating with slender cushions, all bearing small triangular spines; the distal ring lies on the narrow tubular part and consists of 6 cushions of alternating length bearing fine, curved spines. P3 is large, its wall bearing many small spines; the spines are longer on the rounded posterior part near the entrance of P2, and short and often comb-like on the anterior part where it narrows towards P4.

/species/serritermes-serrifer/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This genus is the monotypic genus of the Serritermitidae, and its generic characters are the same as those of the family: in the alate, worker and nymph the apical tooth of the mandibles is proportionally elongate and acute, separated from a single marginal tooth near the ridged molar plate by a broad, curved inner margin, and the family is thereby distinguished from all other termite families; in the soldier the distal portion of both mandibles is long and relatively straight, and the inner margin behind the apex bears numerous coarse serrations; the pronotum is narrow and elongate, with both anterior and posterior margins distinctly bilobed and a deep notch in the centre of each.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is oval, mid light brown to yellow; the fontanelle lies in a small depression, white, of medium size, reduced and bifurcate; the compound eyes are medium-sized and circular, about one quarter of their diameter from the lower margin of the head; the ocelli lie between the compound eyes and the frons and are smaller than the compound eyes; there are 13 or 14 antennal segments; the postclypeus is large, its length slightly less than half its width, with a median longitudinal line; the pronotum is about half as long as wide, its anterior margin slightly concave and its lateral margins rounded and then narrowed posteriorly; each tibia bears 2 apical spurs; the tarsi are 4-segmented; there is no arolium; the cerci are 2-segmented; neither sex has styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The sides of the head are nearly straight and narrow anteriorly, and the head is wider than long (to the postclypeus); the outer margin of the mandibles is concave at the base, nearly straight in the middle and convex towards the apex; the apices of both mandibles are scarcely hooked, and the inner margin of the distal 1/3 bears numerous coarse serrations, with no molar ridges at the base; on the left mandible the serrations extend almost to the base, and before the base there is a blunt swelling and a small tooth-like projection of about 60°; on the right mandible about 6 smaller serrations follow the 3–4 coarse distal ones; the postclypeus is short with a concave anterior margin; the labrum is longer than wide with a bluntly pointed apex; the pronotum is elongate, its anterior and posterior margins deeply notched into two lobes; each tibia bears 2 apical spurs; the tarsi are 4-segmented, the fourth longer than the rest together; there are no styli; the cerci are 2-segmented.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: There are 13 antennal segments; the mandibles are the most specialised known among termites, with the distal portion proportionally elongate and acute and the marginal teeth reduced to a single one.

/species/sinqasapatermes-sachae/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The distal margin of the enteric valve (P2) is not folded into the paunch (P3) but bends towards the ileum (P1), i.e. against the direction of food flow; the armature consists of a ring of 6 equal, nearly triangular ridges, each densely covered with short spines; the armature lies on the outer surface of the cone, facing the inner wall of P1; the valve seating is trilobed and separated from the rest of P3; P3 is subdivided.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. In dorsal view the head capsule is constricted behind the antennal bases, the greatest width lying behind the constriction, at the middle of the posterior lobe; in profile the vertex is nearly straight to the base of the nasus, and the base of the nasus is weakly concave. The nasus is narrow and conical (dorsal view), about as long as the head capsule, and slightly inclined upwards in profile. The mandibles are reduced and lack a point. The postclypeus is moderately arched in profile. The labrum is wider than long with rounded anterolateral corners. There are 11 antennal segments. The pronotum is shallowly saddle-shaped with a rounded, non-concave anterior margin. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: In dorsal view the head capsule is trapezoidal, with the greatest width at the mandibular bases; the fontanelle area is concave and lies in the posterior third of the head capsule. The postclypeus is short and moderately inflated, with a weak median line. There are 12 antennal segments. The pronotum is shallowly saddle-shaped with a rounded, non-concave anterior margin. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. On the left mandible the apical tooth is as large as M1+2 or slightly more prominent, and its posterior margin is weakly concave or truncate; the posterior margin of the apical tooth forms a right or acute angle with the anterior margin of M1+2; the posterior margin of M1+2 is straight or slightly curved; marginal tooth 3 is reduced to a vestige; the molar tooth is visible in the V-shaped gap but its apex is hidden by the molar prominence; the ridges of the molar prominence are very weak. On the right mandible the apical tooth is slightly more prominent than marginal tooth 1, and marginal tooth 2 is invisible or reduced to a minute projection; the molar plate is concave with very weak ridges; the basal notch is distinct. Digestive tract: the gut forms a short, wide coil within the body; the crop is large; the gizzard has a strong muscular layer; the midgut passes along the right side of the body and does not reach the midline in ventral view; the midgut–proctodeum junction is circular, with no mixed segment; the bases of the Malpighian tubules are slightly dilated into ampullae, arranged in adjacent pairs and attached to the inner surface of the junction by a common base; P1 is tubular and shorter than the midgut; P2 lies beneath P1 and is conical, its distal margin bending against the food flow as described under the diagnostic characters; P2 is coaxial with P3; the valve seating is trilobed and separated from the rest of P3 by a constriction; the distal end of P3 is very prominent in dorsal view and joins P4 on the left side; the isthmus is distinct.

/species/sphaerotermes-sphaerothorax/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head rectangular with rounded corners, only slightly narrower anteriorly, reddish yellow, covered with short hairs; left mandible with a much stronger curvature than the right, with several serrations and one blunt tooth near the base; fontanelle central on the head, small and indiscernible. Alate: antennal segment 3 very small, segment 4 about equal to segment 2; neither sex with styli.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular with rounded corners, only slightly narrower anteriorly, reddish yellow, covered with short hairs; antennae 13-segmented (segment 3 smaller than segment 2, segment 2 equal to segment 4); labrum rounded on both sides, with transparent dots; left mandible with a much stronger curvature than the right, with several serrations and one blunt tooth near the base; inner margin of the right mandible smooth; fontanelle central on the head, small and indiscernible; anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave, posterior margin slightly concave. Measurements (mm): head length 1.79–1.83, head width 0.96–1.00, antennae 1.03–1.10, pronotum 0.33–0.37×0.57–0.60, hind tibia 0.61–0.67, left mandible 0.61.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antennae 13-segmented; head width 0.95 mm, hind tibia 0.67 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale brownish yellow, oval; fontanelle a pale circular dot, rather small; head covered with short hairs and a few long bristles; antennal segment 3 very small, segment 4 about equal to segment 2; eyes medium-sized, round, not very close to the lower margin; ocelli large, very close to the eyes; labrum pale, rather transparent; postclypeus concolorous with the head, with a median line, about half as long as wide; pronotum pale yellow, slightly paler than the head, sides rounded, anterior and posterior margins concave, covered with short hairs and long bristles; posterior margins of the meso- and metanotum broadly concave; legs pale yellow, each tibia with two apical spurs; abdominal tergites pale yellow; neither sex with styli. Measurements (mm): head length 1.27–1.28, head width 1.13–1.20, eye diameter 0.30–0.31, pronotum 0.60×0.97–1.07, hind tibia 1.20–1.23, left mandible 0.57; posterior length 26.00, abdominal width 5.00.

/species/spiralitermes-jurupari/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Without soldiers (soldierless). Worker: first proctodaeal segment (P1) extremely long, coiled into a spiral at the end of the abdomen, completing a full turn along the body axis before joining the third proctodaeal segment (P3) on the right side (ventral view); enteric valve seating unlobed, funnel-shaped; enteric valve without spines, but the proximal central region of each of the six symmetrical valves bears a spine directed towards P1 — this ‘spines directed towards P1’ feature distinguishes it from Mangolditermes and Tucupitermes, which likewise have spineless enteric valves.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: External morphology: head capsule pale yellow, with scattered, sparse short hairs; fontanelle conspicuous, oval, white; postclypeus slightly inflated, with only a few short hairs; labrum convex, its hairs coarser than those of the head capsule; antennae 13-segmented (segment 1 > segment 2, segment 3 shorter than the remaining segments). Left mandible with the apical tooth slightly shorter than M1+2, a deep incision between M1+2 and M3 typical of the Neotropical soldierless subfamily, M3 tooth inconspicuous, molar prominence completely concealed by the molar swelling, its process length equal to M1+2; right mandible with the apical tooth longer than M1, an open angle between M1 and M2, M2 tooth triangular, molar plate concave and without grinding ridges. Thorax pale yellow, the margins of the pro-, meso- and metanotum each with a row of long hairs; tibiae and femora slender, of uniform width; anterior surface of the fore coxa with extremely fine, long hairs. Abdomen semi-transparent, each tergite and sternite densely covered with short hairs mostly directed posteriorly. Digestive tract: crop inflated, about 1/4 of the abdominal length; gizzard vestigial; proventricular valve subterminal; midgut uniform, slightly wider in diameter than P1; midgut tongue long, about 1/3 of the midgut length; P1 extremely long, visible on all four surfaces, forming a distinct S shape in left lateral view and a complete loop ventrally, joining P3 at a distinct enteric valve seating (unlobed, funnel-shaped); enteric valve without spines, with six symmetrical valves, the proximal central region of each valve bearing a spine directed towards P1, the spines becoming smaller the further they lie from the valve apex; P3 spherical in ventral view, connected to P4 by a distinct isthmus and forming an inverted U-shaped dorsal loop; P4 smaller in diameter than the midgut, making a short U-shaped turn. Measurements (worker, mm, n=30, means in parentheses): head width 0.68–0.90 (0.80), head length 0.75–0.85 (0.83), hind tibia length 0.73–0.85 (0.78), pronotum width 0.43–0.48 (0.46), fore tibia width/length ratio 0.24–0.36 (0.30).

/species/syncapritermes-greeni/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It shares couplet 13 with Oriencapritermes and is distinguished by the anterior margin of the labrum shallowly concave, the labrum longer than wide and the base of the anterolateral projections without a point; the left mandible has a well-developed, toothed inferior basal process (couplet 12). The fontanelle is small and circular, and the fontanelle gland small.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The anterior margin of the labrum is shallowly concave, the labrum longer than wide, and the base of the anterolateral projections without a point; the left mandible has a well-developed, toothed inferior basal process; the labrum is long; the fontanelle is small and circular, and the fontanelle gland small.

/species/tarditermes-contracolor/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate has a very long apical tooth on the left mandible (index 2.91 according to Emerson and 3.17 according to Sands, the two accounts being inconsistent), marginal tooth 2 absent, and the molar plate without transverse ridges; the postclypeus is 2.1 times as wide as long, the fontanelle is a pale circular spot, the compound eyes project slightly from the sides of the head, and the pronotum is nearly semicircular. The soldier is monotypic: the nasus is long, thick and conical, reaching the large fontanelle at its apex, the mandibles lack a point, the anterior margin of the labrum is wavy, the head capsule is not constricted and in dorsal view is a rounded rectangle that is wider than long to the base of the nasus, and there are 13 antennal segments, setae occurring only at the apex of the nasus together with scattered minute hairs. In the worker the molar plate is weakly concave near the base and the anterior and posterior rounded ridges are more pronounced (index 3.23). Sands notes that its alate is larger than those of all closely related nasute genera except the Neotropical Angularitermes, the closest relative being Mimeutermes; the generic name derives from its extremely sluggish movement.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head, postclypeus and pronotum are covered with fairly dense short hairs but not felted; a few setae occur on the margins of the head, postclypeus and pronotum. The wing membrane is densely covered with short hairs that are longer than those on the wings of most termites. Each abdominal tergite is densely covered with short hairs and bears a row of setae along its posterior margin, each about three times as long as the short hairs; the sternites are more densely haired, the hairs slightly longer than those of the tergites. The head is wide, with the sides nearly parallel near the compound eyes; the compound eyes are large and convex and lie about one seventh to one tenth of their diameter from the lower margin of the head; the ocelli are relatively large, smaller than the antennal sockets and slightly less than their own width from the compound eyes; the fontanelle is a small pale circular spot in the middle of the head; the postclypeus has a dark median line and is slightly more than twice as wide as long; there are 14–15 antennal segments. The apical teeth of the mandibles are very long and the cutting edge behind marginal tooth 1 is reduced; the left mandibular index is 2.91; the right mandible has no marginal tooth 2. The pronotum is large, slightly narrower than the head, with rounded lateral margins and a slightly concave posterior margin; the middle of the mesonotum has a rounded angle of about 130°; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Measurements: head width 1.28–1.35 mm, compound eye diameter 0.41–0.42 mm, forewing 10.15–11.48 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head and frontal projection bear minute hairs visible only in good light; there are no setae except near the apex of the frontal projection; the pronotum has a few short hairs and no setae. The head is relatively large and wide, and the conical frontal projection is thick at its base; the head capsule is not constricted. There are 13 antennal segments, the second and third about equal in length and the fourth slightly shorter than the third. The mandibles lack a point. The pronotum is relatively wide, its anterior margin without a notch or with only a very shallow one, and the anterior region is relatively large. Head length 2.41–2.65 mm, width 1.25–1.49 mm, hind tibia 1.12–1.19 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The mandibles are as in the alate, except that the molar plate of the right mandible is weakly concave near the base and the anterior and posterior rounded ridges are more pronounced; the left mandibular index is 3.23.

/species/tetimatermes-oliveirae/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the 2023 key to workers of the Neotropical soldierless termites this genus forms a couplet of its own (couplet 2) on the character 'fore tibia with a long scoop-shaped excavation' and does not branch further; its other characters overlap with those of related genera.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The fore tibia bears a long scoop-shaped excavation (scooped out excavation, see Fontes 1986).

/species/triangularitermes-triangularice.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is monotypic; it resembles the major soldier of Ngauratermes in size, colour, shape of the head capsule, 13-segmented antennae and the distinct tooth-like projection of the mandibles, and occurs in the same region.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic; the nasus is more conical; the legs and antennae are longer; short hairs on the head capsule are sparse.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The mixed segment is relatively long; the Malpighian tubules are attached in a group at a single point; the end of P1 forms a short loop on the dorsal side; the spines of the two rings of the enteric valve are of similar length.

/species/triclavitermes-catoleensis/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve seating (EVS) forms a distinct ring at the insertion of the enteric valve (EV), followed by a short tube of P3; the ventral surface of the mesenteric tongue bears a white, spherical mesenteric nodule; the enteric valve has three hemispherical sclerotised plates.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic; the head is pale yellow and sparsely covered with setae of the same colour; the head is slightly convex in profile, the postclypeal region inflated and the fontanelle invisible; there are 14 antennal segments, their relative lengths 2>3=4<5; the gizzard is indistinct and without spines, with 4 first-order cushions whose surface bears comb-like scales.

/species/tucupitermes-ubixaba/.note: This genus is monotypic, containing only this species; the following is the genus-level description based on the original literature; species-level measurements and intraspecific variation are given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The cutting edge of the left mandible is twice as long as the distance from the apical tooth to M1+2; the stomodeal valve is twice as long as the crop; the Malpighian ampullae are well developed and visible both in right ventral and in dorsal view; the mesenteric tongue is long and slightly bulbous, reaching the midline of the abdomen; the junction of P1 and P3 is invisible in any view, only a small bilobed seating being visible. This is the largest species currently known in the subfamily (the title of the paper itself refers to the largest Apicotermitinae).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The head capsule is deep yellow with dark longitudinal muscle marks converging towards the vertex; the fontanelle is white, convex and drop-shaped. The head capsule bears few setae of unequal size and none in the posterior region; the postclypeus is small and slightly inflated, with setae as large as those of the head capsule; the labrum is convex, longer than the postclypeus and clypeus together, with relatively thick setae. There are 13 antennal segments, I<II, and III is shorter than the remaining segments. The mandibles are robust: on the left mandible the apical tooth is shorter than M1+2; the distance from the apical tooth to M1+2 is relatively short, and the cutting edge is twice as long as that distance; the notch between M1+2 and M3 is distinct and far from M1+2; M3 is pointed and lies close to the molar prominence; the molar prominence is conical, with grooved sculpture and basal scales. On the right mandible the apical tooth is slightly smaller than M1, and marginal tooth 1 is distinctly larger than the rest; the posterior margin of M1 is wider than the molar prominence; the angle between M1 and M2 is 130°; M2 is conical; the molar plate is concave and without a groove, with grooved sculpture and basal scales. The thorax is pale yellow; the pronotum is wider than half the head width and bears many setae on its margins; the meso- and metanota bear setae on their lateral and posterior margins. The tibiae are paler than the femora and bear many irregular spines on their anterior surface; the front of the fore coxa bears a distinct row of spine-like setae. The abdomen is semi-transparent, its tergites and sternites covered with numerous setae of unequal size. Digestive tract: the crop is small and lies immediately behind the thorax; the gizzard is reduced, without armature, and has 6 primary pulvilli; the stomodeal valve is very long; the midgut has 4 well-developed, slender Malpighian ampullae; P1 is long; P2 is asymmetrical and trilobed; P3 is bulbous and joins P4 through an arched isthmus. Measurements: species-level (Table 1, 20 workers).

/family/hodotermopsidae/.biology: This group inhabits moist forests, boring into damp logs, fallen timber and stumps, and also damages living trees and the timber of cottages and old buildings; hence the name dampwood termites. Primary and secondary forests suffer especially heavily. Their galleries have no connection with the soil, and they live a concealed, wood-dwelling life.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Hodotermitidae)
/family/hodotermopsidae/.diagnosis: The grass termites recorded in the book belong to one of the more primitive branches of the Isoptera. No caste has a fontanelle; the pronotum is flat and narrower than the head; the first tarsomere of the hind leg is cleft only on its ventral surface and remains a single segment dorsally, so that the tarsus appears five-segmented in ventral view but only four-segmented in dorsal view; the cerci consist of four to eight segments; the alate lacks ocelli and has antennae of fifteen to twenty-seven segments; the soldier's tibiae bear two to four apical spurs. The transformed caste (the soldier) approaches the primitive type in head shape, mandibular teeth and the number of antennal and cercal segments; caste differentiation is not pronounced, and many ancestral characters are retained.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.distribution: The book records only one genus and one species as extant in China, found in subtropical montane and hilly forests; the precise localities and hosts are given on the species page for this genus.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.soldier: The soldier of the single genus recorded for China has a broad, flattened, nearly circular head capsule, with the posterior and lateral margins both rounded; the antennae are many-segmented, up to twenty-four segments; the compound eyes are distinct; the mandibles are robust and strongly curved, with very well developed mandibular teeth, the left mandible bearing four marginal teeth and the right three. The pronotum is flat and slightly narrower than the head; the hind tibia bears two lateral spurs in addition to four apical spurs, whereas the fore and mid tibiae have no lateral spurs; the cerci have four to six segments.
/family/hodotermopsidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work follows the system of Snyder and Emerson, placing the subfamily Termopsinae within the family Hodotermitidae (noting that the subfamily had been proposed for elevation to the family Termopsidae). This subfamily was later generally raised to the separate family Hodotermopsidae; this site follows the current system, so what is presented on this page is in fact the part of the original work's Hodotermitidae that concerns the Chinese species.

/family/kalotermitidae/.biology: In all groups of this family both nesting and feeding are confined to wood, and the galleries do not connect with the soil; seasoned timber, standing dead trees, structural timber and stored wooden articles may all be attacked. Because the colonies are small and concealed, they are often noticed only after the wood has been hollowed out; there are comparatively many records of damage to old buildings and old furniture in southern and coastal China.
/family/kalotermitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Kalotermitidae)
/family/kalotermitidae/.diagnosis: This family is a medium-sized, wood-dwelling primitive group, commonly called drywood termites. No caste has a fontanelle; the pronotum is flat, about as wide as the head or slightly wider; the tarsi are four-segmented and the tibiae bear two to four apical spurs; the cerci have only two segments. The soldier retains pale eye spots behind the antennae; the alate has ocelli, the forewing scale is much larger than the hindwing scale and overlies its base, the radial sector is well developed and branches several times, and the subcosta is weak. The family has no worker caste; feeding and brood care are carried out by the nymphs.
/family/kalotermitidae/.distribution: The book records five genera from China (Cryptotermes, Kalotermes, Incisitermes, Glyptotermes and Neotermes); the number of genera and species included here under the current classification has been slightly adjusted; see the list below.

/family/rhinotermitidae/.biology: Most species of this family are both soil- and wood-dwelling, and the nest may be built underground, in tree trunks or within objects on the ground; colony structure is comparatively complex. They feed on living trees, dead wood and structural timber, and can also damage leather, plastics, cable sheathing and even metal articles; several genera are major cosmopolitan pests, causing particularly severe damage to houses, bridges, utility poles and telecommunications installations.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Rhinotermitidae)
/family/rhinotermitidae/.diagnosis: The head bears a fontanelle, the most conspicuous feature of the family; the antennae have thirteen to twenty-five segments; the pronotum is flat and narrower than the head; the tarsi are four-segmented, with no arolium beneath the claws; the cerci have two segments. The alate and worker have three marginal teeth on the left mandible and two on the right, the first marginal tooth bearing a subsidiary tooth; the alate has ocelli, the forewing scale is larger than the hindwing scale and the two overlap, and the wing membrane bears cross-veins forming a network.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.distribution: The family is species-rich and widely distributed, with the Oriental region as its centre of distribution and differentiation; some genera extend into the Neotropical, tropical and Australasian regions, and some species have established populations in the drier parts of the Northern Hemisphere. It occurs throughout China, north and south.
/family/rhinotermitidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work's Rhinotermitidae includes groups that have since been separated or synonymised: the genus Stylotermes is now usually placed in a family of its own, Stylotermitidae; the genus Tsaitermes has been sunk into Reticulitermes; and several species of Coptotermes have also been revised. This site follows the current system, so this page does not correspond genus by genus to the chapter in the original work.

/family/termitidae/.biology: All members of this family are soil-dwelling, nesting underground, in earthen mounds, in tree trunks or inside buildings. Groups such as the Macrotermitinae cultivate fungus combs in the nest to break down wood; they are important decomposers in tropical and subtropical ecosystems and at the same time major pests of crops, forest trees and buildings.
/family/termitidae/.book_ref: (original work, section on the family Termitidae)
/family/termitidae/.diagnosis: The largest family in the Isoptera, comprising about three-quarters of all species; its members are soil-dwelling higher termites, nesting mostly underground or within earthen mounds. The book divides it into five subfamilies: the Termitinae, the Amitermitinae, the Macrotermitinae, the Nasutitermitinae, and the Apicotermitinae established separately by Grasse and Noirot in 1954. Soldiers and workers are often markedly polymorphic, and a few groups lack soldiers. The soldier's pronotum is narrower than the head, its anterior margin upturned and saddle-shaped; a fontanelle is present; the cerci have one to two segments and the tarsi three to four. The alate has only one or two marginal teeth on the left mandible; the forewing and hindwing scales are separate, the forewing scale slightly larger; the radial vein is reduced or lost; the postclypeus is large and convex, and the fontanelle is prominent.
/family/termitidae/.distribution: The family is most flourishing in the tropics and subtropics; southern China is rich in species, and it is distributed throughout the provinces and regions south of the Yangtze River, being especially concentrated in the mountains of South China and the Southwest.
/family/termitidae/.taxonomy_note: The original work adopts the five-subfamily system and leaves within this family such groups as the genus Indotermes, which have since been proposed for separate family rank; this site follows the current system, so this page is an adapted account of the general characters of the original work's Termitidae, and the placement of individual genera follows the list.

/genus/ahmaditermes/.alate: In the alate, the apical tooth of the left mandible is almost as long as the first and second marginal teeth together, and the cutting edge between the marginal teeth is undulating. Antennae 15-segmented. The media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, while that of the hindwing arises from the base of the radial sector. These mandibular and wing-venation characters agree with those seen in the worker; only the number of antennal segments is greater.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Ahmaditermes section of the original book)
/genus/ahmaditermes/.diagnosis: In the soldier the head lacks a nasus and is broadly pear-shaped; the head surface is scattered with fine hairs; the head is constricted behind the antennal sockets, the sides strongly convex near the base, the posterior margin concave at the middle; the mandibles are short and blunt, without pointed tips; the mandibular body is robust; monomorphic or dimorphic; antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed in southern China, mostly in tropical and subtropical forest areas.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.soldier: Soldier monomorphic or dimorphic. Head surface scattered with fine hairs. Head without a nasus, broadly pear-shaped in outline, narrowed behind the antennal sockets, the sides distinctly swollen near the base, the posterior margin concave inwards at the middle. Mandibles short and blunt, not forming pointed tips at the apex, the mandibular body robust. Antennae 12–13-segmented. The head capsule is widest between the swellings near the base.
/genus/ahmaditermes/.worker: In the worker the apical tooth of the left mandible is almost as long as the first and second marginal teeth together, and the cutting edge between the two marginal teeth is undulating rather than straight. Its mandibular tooth pattern agrees with that of the alate; only the body form and the development of the wings differ.

/genus/ancistrotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Ancistrotermes section of the original book)
/genus/ancistrotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier dimorphic, predominantly yellow in colour; head nearly circular, widest at the middle; the anterior portion of the mandibles slender and curved; the inner margin with only minute denticles at mid-length; labrum ligulate with a bluntly rounded apex; antennae 15- or 16-segmented; pronotum distinctly narrower than the head width.
/genus/ancistrotermes/.distribution: Oriental and Afrotropical regions; distributed in tropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/ancistrotermes/.soldier: Soldier of two forms, major and minor. In the major soldier the head capsule is yellow to deep yellow, the mandibles reddish brown, the labrum pale yellow, the antennae milky white, and the pronotum, abdomen and legs pale yellow. Long hairs are scattered over the head, the labrum bears a pair of apical hairs, and several long hairs are arranged in longitudinal rows on each side. The head is nearly circular to oval, widest at the middle, the middle or anterior part humped in lateral view. Labrum ligulate with a bluntly rounded apex; the anterior portion of the mandibles slender and curved, the inner margin with or without a minute denticle at mid-length. Postmentum raised, projecting in a broad arc at the middle. When the antennae are 15-segmented the third segment is the shortest; when 16-segmented the fourth is the shortest. The pronotum is narrower than the head, its anterior and posterior margins both concave at the middle. The minor soldier is paler in colour and smaller in size, its parts otherwise similar to those of the major soldier.

/genus/arcotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Arcotermes section of the original book)
/genus/arcotermes/.diagnosis: In the soldier the head bears only scattered short hairs; head pear-shaped; distinctly narrowed behind the antennal sockets, widest near the posterior margin; posterior margin rounded, scarcely concave at the middle; nasus a slender tube; mandibles short and small, blunt, without pointed tips; antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/arcotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; a component of tropical and subtropical areas, recorded from southern China.
/genus/arcotermes/.soldier: Soldier with sparse pilosity on the head. Head pear-shaped, the lateral margins markedly narrowed behind the antennal sockets, widening again only from there backwards to near the posterior margin, widest near the posterior margin; posterior margin arcuate, not or scarcely concave at the middle. Nasus tubular. Mandibles without pointed tips. Antennae 12–13-segmented.
/genus/arcotermes/.worker: Worker with a large and conspicuous fontanelle situated near the middle of the vertex; the cutting edge between the first and second marginal teeth of the left mandible is not straight but undulating, and the undulation is gentle, an easily observed character of the worker of this genus.

/genus/coptotermes/.alate: Alate with a broad, oval head capsule; postclypeus very short, its surface flat. Antennae 18–25-segmented. Pronotum flattened, narrower than the head capsule. Forewing scale larger than the hindwing scale and overlapping it; venation with a very faint reticulate pattern, the wing surface hairy; the media of the forewing arises independently at the humeral suture, that of the hindwing from the base of the radial sector, the media and cubitus very close together. Fontanelle situated at the centre of the head.
/genus/coptotermes/.biology: Species of this genus mainly attack timber components in buildings and cause the greatest losses of any termite group in the provinces of southern China; buried plastic cables and amenity trees are also frequently damaged. They are important pests worldwide. The species are morphologically very similar and often difficult to identify, and individuals of different colony ages in the same nest differ greatly in colour and size.
/genus/coptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Coptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/coptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with an oval head, distinctly narrowed anteriorly; fontanelle a large opening, situated at the front of the head and projecting forwards as a short tube; mandibles slender and curved, the inner margin smooth and toothless apart from the serrate notch at the base; antennae 13–17-segmented.
/genus/coptotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; distributed throughout the provinces of southern China, with the greatest number of species in the South China area.
/genus/coptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with an oval head, markedly narrowed anteriorly. Fontanelle large, situated at the front of the head, extending outwards as a short tube with the opening directed forwards. Mandibles slender and curved, the tooth row entirely absent apart from the serrate notch retained at the base, the inner margin smooth. Antennae 13–17-segmented. Labrum an acute ligula. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head capsule.

/genus/cryptotermes/.alate: Alate head pale yellow, yellowish brown, reddish brown or dark brown in colour, pilosity sparse to moderate, posterior margin evenly rounded, coronal suture usually visible. Compound eyes small, round or nearly round; ocelli oval, touching or close to the compound eyes. Antennae 12–18-segmented. Postclypeus slightly trapezoidal, its anterior margin either convex or concave; labrum transverse. Left mandible with three marginal teeth, the right with two. Pronotum narrower than the head capsule, in a few species slightly exceeding the width of the head including the compound eyes. Tibiae with three apical spurs, tarsi 4-segmented.
/genus/cryptotermes/.book_ref: (genus-level account reorganised and rewritten from the Cryptotermes section of the original book)
/genus/cryptotermes/.diagnosis: Soldier with a short, thick head capsule, the front part almost black; frontal and genal regions each extending into a pair of horn-like processes; vertex and frontal area often irregularly wrinkled; antennae 11–15-segmented; postclypeus nearly trapezoidal; tarsi 4-segmented; cerci 2-segmented.
/genus/cryptotermes/.distribution: Oriental region; species of this genus are recorded from all provinces of southern China.
/genus/cryptotermes/.soldier: Soldier with a short, thick head, dark brown with the front part almost black; in some species the vertex, frontal area and sides are coarsely wrinkled, and a thick transverse frontal ridge often lies between vertex and frontal area, with or without a V-shaped notch at its centre. Two pairs of horn-like processes at the front of the head: the upper pair, above and in front of the antennal sockets, arises from the lateral margin of the postclypeus and is termed the frontal horn; the lower pair, below and in front of the antennal sockets, is formed by prolongation of the genae and is termed the genal horn, its shape varying with the species. Frontal surface mostly concave; compound eyes generally visible, unpigmented. Antennae 11–15-segmented, clypeus slightly trapezoidal, labrum nearly triangular or ligulate. Mandibles short, the outer margin convex at the middle, the posterior part of the postmentum broad. Pronotum about as wide as the head capsule, its anterior margin deeply concave, mostly wavy or dentate. Legs short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented, cerci 2-segmented.

/genus/cucurbitermes/.alate: Dealate head with long and short hairs interspersed with setae, the pronotum with rather many setae. Head nearly circular; fontanelle large and elongate-oval, not forked anteriorly, with a longitudinal line running from it to the posterior margin; postclypeus raised, with another longitudinal line at its centre; compound eyes large, elliptical and convex outwards, ocelli oval and slightly convex. Apical tooth of the left mandible as long as the first marginal tooth, the cutting edge between the two teeth nearly straight. Antennae 15-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum nearly straight, the posterior margin slightly concave at the middle. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented.
